artigo.texto: Previsão do preço das ações da Bloom Energy: escassez de energia em data centers de IA impulsiona demanda por células de combustível, ação pode subir para US$ 309 As ações da Bloom Energy dispararam 86% entre 29 de julho e 25 de setembro, impulsionadas pela crise energética nos data centers de inteligência artificial. Com gargalos na rede elétrica e longos prazos de entrega para turbinas tradicionais, a geração "atrás do medidor" ganhou força. Embora apresentem custo nivelado superior, as células de combustível da empresa destacam-se pela rápida entrega, de 6 a 12 meses. Tecnicamente, a ação sofre uma correção na tendência de alta, testando a média móvel de 20 dias, com suporte crítico no nível de retração de Fibonacci de 0,5 (US$ 254,28). TradingKey - As ações da Bloom Energy (BE) atingiram uma máxima recente de US$ 292,72 em 25 de setembro. Apenas dois meses antes, em 29 de julho, os papéis da fabricante de células de combustível custavam apenas US$ 157, representando um ganho impressionante de 86% no período. Ela não apenas superou significativamente o índice Nasdaq Composite e o índice Philadelphia Semiconductor no mesmo período, mas também ficou à frente de ações populares de memória — a SanDisk (SNDK) subiu cerca de 62%, e a Micron (MU) avançou aproximadamente 32%. Então, o que permitiu a essa empresa superar significativamente o mercado durante o boom de investimentos em IA? Os data centers de IA enfrentam atualmente um problema prático: é possível comprar os chips, mas a conexão com a rede elétrica nem sempre é simples. A expansão lenta da rede e os longos prazos de entrega de equipamentos de geração de energia tornam o 'fornecimento de energia o mais rápido possível' uma consideração central na aquisição de eletricidade. Como resultado, o setor de células de combustível, no qual a Bloom Energy atua, vem ganhando novas oportunidades de crescimento. Autoprodução de Energia Acelera Expansão De acordo com projeções do Goldman Sachs, a demanda global por eletricidade em data centers crescerá 170% até 2030 em comparação com 2025, com mais de 60% do crescimento incremental vindo dos Estados Unidos. No entanto, a construção da rede elétrica está significativamente atrasada. A extensão média anual de novas linhas de transmissão de alta tensão construídas nos EUA caiu de 1.700 milhas em 2010–2014 para 350 milhas em 2020–2023. Para os projetos de conexão à rede listados no relatório, o tempo mediano de espera entre a solicitação e a operação comercial é de quase cinco anos. Essa espera significa que uma infraestrutura de computação cara não pode ser colocada em uso. Consequentemente, os data centers estão começando a implantar equipamentos de geração de energia no próprio local ou nas proximidades, conceito conhecido como "geração atrás do medidor". O Goldman Sachs elevou sua previsão para 2030 da capacidade global de geração atrás do medidor em data centers de 40 GW para 67 GW, estimando que ela poderá atender a cerca de 25% da demanda de energia dos data centers globais até lá. Alguns operadores chegaram a assinar contratos de fornecimento de energia de até 15 anos, tornando a geração no local um arranjo de longo prazo. A Competitividade da Bloom Energy Reside na Velocidade de Entrega A Bloom Energy é uma fabricante de células de combustível de óxido sólido. Segundo comparações do Goldman Sachs, as células de combustível não possuem vantagem de custo: em um modelo que estima um data center de 500 megawatts, seu custo nivelado de eletricidade ao longo do ciclo de vida é de aproximadamente US$ 117/MWh, superior aos US$ 80 de motores alternativos e aos US$ 81 de turbinas a gás de ciclo combinado. Mesmo assumindo um crédito tributário de investimento de 30% sob as premissas do Goldman Sachs, o custo das células de combustível cai apenas para cerca de US$ 90. Um dos principais motivos pelos quais os clientes ainda estão dispostos a considerá-las é a velocidade de entrega. Segundo relatos, os fabricantes de células de combustível de óxido sólido estimam cerca de 6 a 12 meses desde a realização do pedido até o fornecimento de energia, enquanto motores alternativos exigem de 1,5 a 2,5 anos e turbinas a gás de grande porte exigem de 5 a 7 anos. Para projetos de IA ávidos por entrar em operação, um fornecimento de energia antecipado significa disponibilizar capacidade computacional mais cedo e gerar receita antes. Na pontuação geral do Goldman Sachs, o prazo de comissionamento representa 20% e a disponibilidade responde por 15%; consequentemente, as células de combustível receberam a pontuação mais alta. Escassez generalizada de equipamentos de energia traz oportunidades de expansão para a BE A oportunidade para as células a combustível também decorre de gargalos de oferta em outros equipamentos de geração de energia. De acordo com dados de referência, a carteira de pedidos combinada e a capacidade reservada da GE Vernova atingem 116 gigawatts, com a capacidade totalmente vendida até 2030. Os motores alternativos também enfrentam longos tempos de espera: os pedidos da Cummins estão reservados até 2028, enquanto a carteira de pedidos e a capacidade reservada da INNIO superam 15 gigawatts. Consequentemente, os operadores de data centers precisam avaliar simultaneamente múltiplas opções de suprimento de energia. Por outro lado, o Goldman Sachs acredita que os reatores nucleares modulares de pequeno porte têm potencial de longo prazo para geração local de energia, mas, devido aos restritivos prazos de construção, uma implantação em larga escala é improvável antes de 2030. Antes disso, turbinas a gás, motores alternativos e células a combustível continuarão a atender conjuntamente à demanda incremental. A oportunidade para a BE torna-se, assim, clara: a lentidão na interconexão com a rede elétrica e o atraso na entrega de equipamentos tradicionais elevam o valor comercial da implantação rápida de energia. artigo.texto: Mercado global de distribuição de energia 380V 400V: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de distribuição de energia 380V 400V até 2035: crescimento se acelera com a demanda de data centers e renováveis Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de distribuição de energia 380V 400V, o mercado chega a 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de distribuição de energia 380V 400V entra em uma fase de expansão sustentada, com a demanda projetada para crescer a uma taxa composta de 6–9% ao ano até 2035. Esse crescimento se apoia em três forças estruturais: a rápida expansão de data centers e de projetos de escala utilitária, a integração de energias renováveis e de sistemas de armazenamento em baterias e a eletrificação industrial em curso. A Ásia-Pacífico segue como centro de gravidade tanto da produção quanto do consumo, respondendo por quase metade da produção mundial e por parcela semelhante da demanda. As cadeias de suprimento regionais, porém, estão se redesenhando, com fabricantes ampliando capacidade de montagem na América do Norte e no Oriente Médio para reduzir prazos de entrega e atender a exigências de conteúdo local. O mercado também passa por uma atualização tecnológica: painéis de distribuição inteligentes, com medição integrada, proteção contra arco elétrico e monitoramento remoto, conquistam participação crescente em projetos de grande porte e alcançam prêmios de preço de 30–60% sobre as configurações básicas. Ao mesmo tempo, a volatilidade dos custos de matérias-primas e os prazos prolongados de componentes representam riscos para margens e fornecimento. Este relatório oferece uma perspectiva baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, arquitetura da demanda, dinâmica competitiva e tendências regionais até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de distribuição de energia 380V 400V prevê crescimento constante até 2035, com a demanda global avançando a uma taxa composta de 6–9% ao ano. Essa projeção pressupõe continuidade dos investimentos em infraestrutura de rede, projetos de energia renovável e data centers, além de despesas de capital industrial moderadas. A Ásia-Pacífico continuará sendo o maior mercado, sustentada por polos manufatureiros na China, na Índia e no Sudeste Asiático, mas o crescimento também se acelerará na América do Norte e na Europa, à medida que a infraestrutura envelhecida for modernizada e a digitalização das redes de baixa tensão ganhar ritmo. O índice de mercado (2025=100) deve alcançar 185 em 2035, refletindo uma quase duplicação da atividade de mercado no período de previsão. Entre as principais incertezas estão a volatilidade dos preços de matérias-primas, sobretudo cobre e aço, e o ritmo de harmonização das normas entre as regiões. Ainda assim, os vetores fundamentais da demanda — eletrificação, descarbonização e digitalização — são robustos, e espera-se que o mercado supere o crescimento industrial mais amplo. A migração para equipamentos de distribuição inteligentes continuará a remodelar portfólios de produtos e posicionamento competitivo, com ganho de participação para fornecedores capazes de oferecer soluções integradas, em conformidade com as normas e com entrega rápida. Vetores e restrições da demanda Principais vetores de demanda - Expansão acelerada de data centers e infraestrutura de nuvem, que exige distribuição de energia 380V/400V confiável para servidores, refrigeração e sistemas de backup. - Integração de energias renováveis e armazenamento em baterias, em que usinas solares e eólicas precisam de distribuição CA de baixa tensão dedicada para inversores e cargas auxiliares. - Eletrificação e automação industrial, com fábricas migrando para a manufatura inteligente e substituindo processos a combustível fóssil por alternativas elétricas. - Investimentos em modernização e resiliência da rede, sobretudo na América do Norte e na Europa, para substituir equipamentos envelhecidos e melhorar a confiabilidade. - Digitalização da distribuição de baixa tensão, com disjuntores e sistemas de monitoramento habilitados para IoT especificados em 20–30% dos grandes projetos. - Regionalização das cadeias de suprimento, levando fabricantes a estabelecer montagem local na América do Norte e no Oriente Médio para atender às regras de conteúdo local. Possíveis restrições ao crescimento - Volatilidade dos custos de matérias-primas, especialmente cobre e aço galvanizado, que pressiona margens e complica licitações de preço fixo. - Prazos prolongados para componentes especializados, como disjuntores em caixa moldada, limitando a produção de integradores de pequeno e médio porte. - Divergências de normas de segurança e desempenho entre regiões (IEC, UL, AS/NZS), elevando os custos de qualificação para fornecedores globais. - Escassez de mão de obra qualificada para instalação e comissionamento, sobretudo em projetos de renováveis e data centers em rápido crescimento. - Concorrência intensa de produtores de baixo custo, especialmente nos segmentos de linha padrão, limitando o poder de precificação dos fornecedores premium. Estrutura da demanda por indústria de uso final Infraestrutura de rede (participação estimada: 30%) A infraestrutura de rede continua sendo o maior setor de uso final da distribuição de energia 380V/400V, respondendo por cerca de 30% da demanda global. Esse segmento abrange subestações de transmissão e distribuição, postes de derivação e quadros de baixa tensão que conectam redes de média tensão aos usuários finais. artigo.texto: O Brasil representa um dos maiores e mais cobiçados mercados do mundo para o segmento de duas rodas. De olho nesse potencial, a CFMoto estruturou uma entrada agressiva no País. Para afastar o antigo estigma de falta de peças associado a marcas chinesas, a fabricante formou um amplo estoque de reposição antes de iniciar as vendas. Com o pós-venda garantido, a marca vem consolidando sua presença nas categorias trail, naked e custom. Por que a CFMoto Ibex 450 atrai tanta atenção O símbolo dessa nova fase é a Ibex 450, uma das motocicletas mais comentadas do ano. O interesse do público é massivo, alimentado pelos elogios ao nível de equipamentos e preço competitivo. Ao examinar a moto de perto, a montagem impressiona. A qualidade das soldas do chassi é impecável e a receita foi pensada para o off-road real. O motor bicilíndrico de 450,06 cm³, com virabrequim a 270 graus, garante um torque forte desde as baixas rotações, traduzindo-se em força imediata e tração para superar obstáculos. A configuração forma um dos pacotes mais competitivos do segmento, trazendo rodas de 21 polegadas na dianteira e 18 na traseira. O grande diferencial está na suspensão Kayaba (KYB). Enquanto a concorrência peca na regulagem, a CFMoto entrega um conjunto ajustável, permitindo uma calibragem que absorve impactos sem pancadas secas de fim de curso. Comprovando essa robustez, a Ibex 450 venceu sua categoria no Red Bull Romaniacs com chassi e motor originais de fábrica. CFMoto Ibex 450: ela rouba vendas da Himalayan 450 e da Honda NX500? | Teste A CFMoto Ibex 450 chegou ao Brasil para disputar um dos segmentos mais interessantes do mercado de motocicletas. Com motor bicilíndrico de 450 cm³, 44 cv de pot. Crédito: Estadão O pacote tecnológico não fica devendo a motos superiores. A Ibex 450 vem de série com controle de tração, bolha com regulagem de altura e painel TFT colorido vertical. Além disso, conta com diversos acessórios, como bancos com aquecimento. O design segue a linha do portfólio oficial da marca no Brasil, que conta com a trail Ibex 450, a aventureira Ibex 700, a naked 450NK (apresentada no Suhai Festival Interlagos) e as custom com a 450CL-C e a 450CL-C Bobber. Todas têm o design assinado pelo estúdio austríaco Kiska, responsável por desenhar as icônicas KTM. A mecânica de ponta também é regra: eletrônica Bosch, embreagem deslizante e freios J.Juan (divisão da italiana Brembo). CFMoto tem alta demanda, mas oferta restrita O desafio atual é o volume de entrega. O produto gerou um impacto tão expressivo que a procura atingiu níveis raros no mercado. Apenas para a Ibex 450, há mais de 60 mil registros de intenção de compra direta, dado revelado por Urano Carvalho, head de operações de motos da CFMoto Brasil, durante o Festival Interlagos. Devido a essa alta demanda, as vendas ainda ocorrem em lotes. Essa dinâmica força a movimentação de um mercado acomodado. A motocicleta chinesa de padrão premium já está no Brasil, oferecendo tecnologia por um preço coerente. Essa competitividade beneficia o consumidor e, quem não se ajustar rapidamente, perderá espaço. Carregando ofertas... Os comentários são exclusivos para cadastrados.

artigo.texto: SPOKANE, Wash. — The "Aquifers over AI" rally in Spokane on Sunday called for a statewide pause on new data centers, as organizers raised concerns about the impacts on water use and strain on local infrastructure. The event on Sunday was part of the Statewide Day of Action, where activists from across the state hosted rallies in many cities, demanding a statewide moratorium on new data center construction. Organizers said the push centered on protecting groundwater resources because they believed growing AI infrastructure could affect the city's aquifer. About 100 people attended the rally. Guest speakers from environmental nonprofit organizations also took part. The group started at the Riverfront Park Rotary Fountain, marched past City Hall and the Public Works building, and crossed the Monroe Street Bridge. Organizers said they wanted more transparency about the strain data centers place on regional infrastructure, noise pollution, and calls for more local and statewide moratoriums on new data centers. One of the organizers said the effort needed to go beyond Spokane and involve other communities. "Like, sure, it's great to pass in the city, but they're not going to build one here. It's going to be in the county. It's going to be in another city. Like this is why it's important that we build a coalition. We work with other jurisdictions; we work statewide to pass this moratorium," said Zenthia Peterson. Organizers also said the Spokane River was running the driest it had ever been and argued new data centers could make that worse. They said they hoped the turnout would send a message in support of a statewide moratorium against new data centers.

artigo.texto: BYD's Global EV Lead Widens to 276,000 Units Over Tesla as Shares Buckle Under Asian Risk-Off Wave Published on 10/03/2026 at 08:20 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD has stretched its advantage over Tesla in the pure-electric vehicle race to roughly 276,000 units, after the Chinese manufacturer delivered 762,478 battery-only passenger cars worldwide in the third quarter of 2026, against 486,532 from its US rival over the same stretch. The widening gap underscores how decisively the balance of power has shifted in the BEV segment, with Tesla leaning on a demand rebound in Europe while BYD pushed its own electric ramp-up at full throttle. That momentum carried into BYD's broader numbers. Total deliveries of new-energy vehicles reached 1,323,065 units in the third quarter, an 18.8% year-on-year advance that snapped a run of four consecutive quarters of annual declines. September alone accounted for 463,561 alternative-drive sales, up 16.98% from a year earlier, with overseas markets doing the heavy lifting — exports of passenger cars and pick-ups surged 153.9% to 179,877 units during the month, according to Reuters. Exports Offset a Soft Home Market For the first nine months of the year, BYD shipped close to 1.343 million vehicles abroad, a jump of 92.7%, a performance that has become the company's principal buffer against weakness at home. Cumulative global deliveries over that period stood at 3,131,576 units, still 3.94% below the prior-year level. The domestic picture remains the sore spot. Nomura flagged that both Chinese demand and order backlogs fell short of expectations, while aggressive competition from local players such as Leapmotor and Geely keeps established manufacturers under pressure. Geely, for its part, is pressing ahead with new systems designed to shorten charging times, sharpening the technological contest among Chinese brands. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? JPMorgan Steps Back Analysts have been recalibrating accordingly. JPMorgan downgraded the stock from "Overweight" to "Neutral" on September 30 and cut its price target to 88 HK$ from 124 HK$, citing subdued domestic demand in China, higher procurement costs, regulatory uncertainty and trade barriers in overseas operations. The market's mood has followed suit. On Friday the shares closed 2.4% lower at EUR 8.39, dragged down by broad weakness across Asian trading venues rather than any company-specific catalyst. Surging US Treasury yields and rising oil prices dented risk appetite in Hong Kong, according to media reports and Reuters. Year-to-date, the stock is down 22%, and it now trades only about 4.5% above its 52-week low of EUR 8.03. New Model, Same Old Margin Question Even with the share price under pressure, BYD continues to broaden its line-up. The ten-millionth vehicle from its Dynasty series, the Da Han, rolled off the production line, with its official market launch set for October 13. Investors, though, are increasingly focused on profitability rather than volume. The fear of sustained margin compression from the industry's bruising price war has taken center stage, and preserving earnings power through a global expansion under tougher conditions looms as the company's defining challenge. O mercado global de argamassas à base de cimento entra em uma fase de expansão sustentada, com a demanda projetada para crescer a uma taxa composta anual de 4–6% entre 2026 e 2035. Esse crescimento é sustentado pelo aumento dos investimentos em infraestrutura de fabricação de eletrônicos, incluindo fábricas de semicondutores, data centers e instalações de montagem de precisão, onde as argamassas à base de cimento são essenciais para amortecimento de vibrações, estabilidade térmica e alinhamento preciso de equipamentos. As argamassas de alto desempenho, formuladas com modificadores poliméricos e aditivos especiais, representam 25–35% do valor do mercado global e avançam 6–8% ao ano, superando as formulações padrão. A Ásia-Pacífico segue como o maior polo de consumo e produção, respondendo por 45–55% do consumo global, enquanto o Oriente Médio e a África dependem fortemente de importações. Este relatório oferece uma perspectiva baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, segmentação, dinâmica da cadeia de suprimentos e posicionamento competitivo até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de argamassas à base de cimento prevê crescimento constante entre 2026 e 2035, com o consumo global avançando a uma taxa composta anual de 4–6%. Essa trajetória pressupõe a continuidade dos investimentos de capital em fabricação de semicondutores, data centers e automação industrial, além das atividades de manutenção e modernização de infraestrutura. As argamassas de grau padrão, usadas na construção geral e na alvenaria, crescerão 3–4% ao ano, enquanto as formulações de alto desempenho para aplicações de precisão avançarão 6–8%, ampliando sua participação no valor total do mercado. A Ásia-Pacífico continuará sendo a região dominante, sustentada pelos polos de fabricação de eletrônicos na China, em Taiwan, na Coreia do Sul e no Sudeste Asiático. América do Norte e Europa registrarão crescimento moderado, impulsionado pela repatriação de manufaturas críticas e pela modernização das redes elétricas. A América Latina e o Oriente Médio e África apresentarão maior dependência de importações, com a demanda atrelada a projetos de construção e energia de grande porte. artigo.texto: Volkswagen Rewires Battery Supply and Model Lineup as Margins Hit a Wall Published on 10/04/2026 at 19:20 | Editorial boerse-global.de Volkswagen is pressing ahead with a sweeping overhaul of how it builds cars and where it sources their batteries, even as the financial picture darkens. The Wolfsburg group has locked in a trio of battery joint ventures, signaled the arrival of an electric Tiguan, and opened a new round of labor talks — all while its shares scrape the bottom of a 52-week range. Three joint ventures, one trimmed stake Under an agreement dated September 28, Volkswagen Group, its in-house battery unit PowerCo SE and China's Gotion High-tech will establish three separate joint companies. The ventures will turn out LFP battery cells and cathode material at plants in Valencia, Spain; Šurany, Slovakia; and Kenitra, Morocco. The partners also plan to pool procurement and sales efforts across Europe. As part of the same arrangement, Volkswagen signed a binding deal to offload 5.3 percent of its holding in Gotion. The group will keep a meaningful stake once the transaction closes. Paris as a stage The battery pacts sit alongside a broader push to shore up its European base. On Thursday, ahead of an industry gathering in France, Volkswagen unveiled its "For Europe" initiative, pledging to strengthen European supply chains and safeguard future-proof jobs. Investment will concentrate on electric mobility, battery technology, software and artificial intelligence. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Volkswagen? A political and media exchange is set for Paris on October 11, followed the next day by the Paris Motor Show, where the Volkswagen, Audi, Škoda, CUPRA and Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles brands will roll out new models. Back home, the company confirmed the October debut of the ID. Tiguan, with the model's actual market launch slated for early 2027. Contracts on the table Labor relations form the other front. On Wednesday, management gave notice on several collective agreements effective December 31, 2026, while explicitly exempting the future collective agreement that guarantees job security. Revision talks have already begun, with further sessions with IG Metall scheduled for the second half of October. A warning that reset expectations These moves are unfolding against a sharply weaker backdrop. In mid-September, Volkswagen cut its full-year 2026 guidance, projecting revenue of roughly EUR 315 billion and an operating margin of up to 1 percent. The company had previously targeted a margin of 4.0 to 5.5 percent. Management blamed restructuring costs, a tough market in China and a non-cash write-down of about EUR 6 billion on Porsche. Sentiment took a further hit roughly a week ago when Germany's KBA federal transport authority ordered a recall over a potentially corrosion-prone steering screw. Volkswagen at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Analysts trim their targets The revisions have rippled through brokerages. On September 21, Kepler Cheuvreux's Michael Raab downgraded the stock from "Buy" to "Hold" and cut his price target to EUR 80 from EUR 92, citing the reduced valuation headroom after the profit warning. That same day, DZ Bank's Michael Punzet lowered his fair value to EUR 73 from EUR 75, keeping a "Hold" rating and pointing to the reduced margin forecast for the year and more demanding targets through the end of the decade. A stock near its floor The market has taken notice. The shares are down 35 percent since the start of the year, and on Friday they closed at EUR 67.60 — barely above the fresh 52-week low of EUR 67.22 touched during the session. Investors will get a fuller read on October 29, when Volkswagen publishes its interim report for the first nine months. artigo.texto: Carbon tax deferment gives ministry more time to finalise regulatory, policy framework, says Arthur KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The deferment of the carbon tax implementation is aligned with the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry’s efforts to establish a complete regulatory and policy framework before enforcing emission caps. Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the government decided to delay the tax, originally planned for this year, following global geopolitical developments that led to volatile energy prices, providing affected industries with a necessary buffer. Speaking during a Concorde Club dialogue session at Wisma Bernama on Monday, he said the postponement is also timely as the ministry works towards solidifying the required legal structure, including the National Carbon Market Policy and the upcoming Climate Change Act. “[The postponement] is also right because we need to have the proper framework and all that in place first. That’s why we’ve been successful in launching the National Carbon Market Policy and I hope that we can table the Climate Change Act soon. “Once that is up, then we have the framework and the policies all clearly in place, including the regulation, enforcement, the regulatory powers to give us to set the emission ceiling, and then we can know anything above the ceiling, then the carbon tax will come into place as a penalty to the polluters. “So, we’re not looking at this year for the carbon tax,” he said. Meanwhile, on Clean Air Regulations exemption, Arthur said exemptions for industrial plants under the regulation would only be extended to factory operators who demonstrate proactive measures toward technology adoption. He said while no new blanket extensions are being issued, factory operators whose exemptions expire by January next year must show clear steps toward compliance, with 2030 set as the final deadline for total compliance across all industries. “We had the Clean Air Regulations, which came into force in 2014, where plants, factories are not allowed to pollute above the 600 milligram per cubic metre...that was the regulation set...however, they have been enjoying exemptions up to this year. “So when I came in as the minister, I decided that I will not be issuing any more exemptions because the technology is available, the technology is accessible and if we are to meet our target of net zero emissions by 2050, we need to have all this in place and we definitely need the cooperation from the industries as well,” he said. He added that while operators need adequate time for feasibility studies and modifications, strict progress is required to qualify for temporary extensions. The session, titled “Building A Resilient Malaysia: Environment, Climate And Our Future”, was moderated by Bernama chairman Datuk Seri Wong Chun Wai. Also present was Bernama chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, as well as members of the local and foreign media based in Malaysia. artigo.texto: Companies Strengthen Position in Data Center Market Through Long-Term Chiller Partnership Supporting More Than 5GW of AI Data Center Capacity News Summary - LG Electronics has secured a long-term supply agreement with AIR Control Concepts to provide advanced cooling solutions for AI data centers in North America. - The agreement supports a large-scale, multi-year chiller supply program supporting data centers with more than 5GW of capacity. - This milestone reflects AIR's confidence in LG's cooling technologies to meet the demanding standards required for hyperscale data center infrastructure, positioning LG as a key supplier in this market. - For AIR, the partnership reinforces its position as one of North America's fastest-growing AI data center infrastructure platforms. NORFOLK, Va., Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LG Electronics USA has signed a major supply agreement with AIR Control Concepts (AIR), the largest global platform of leading HVAC, electrical, service, and controls companies, to provide advanced chillers for data centers in the United States and Canada. The long-term contract builds on AIR's role as a leading AI data center (AIDC) platform provider and accelerates LG's expansion into the global AIDC cooling market, addressing the rapidly growing demand for high-efficiency thermal management solutions in AI infrastructure. Securing AI Infrastructure Partnership with Leading Data Center Developers Under the agreement, LG will supply advanced chillers supporting large-scale AI data center projects exceeding 5GW of capacity in North America. AIR oversees mega-scale infrastructure projects across major North American data center hubs, serving leading global data center operators as key customers. The LG Air-Cooled Centrifugal Chiller designed for AI data centers incorporates refrigerant free-cooling technology, using cool outdoor air to lower the compressor cooling load. Based on LG's internal simulation, refrigerant free-cooling can consume approximately 30 percent less energy annually than waterside free-cooling.1 This contract demonstrates that LG's cooling solutions meet AIR's stringent technical and reliability requirements for its hyperscale data center projects. Moving beyond single-project bids, the agreement establishes LG as a core infrastructure partner supporting the growth of AI data centers in North America. For AIR, the partnership reinforces its position as one of North America's fastest-growing AI data center infrastructure platforms. As data center customers race to bring new capacity online, AIR is scaling the operational depth and supplier relationships needed to deliver mission-critical cooling infrastructure on schedule and at the standard the industry now requires. Targeting Rapid Growth in the Global AIDC Market The expansion of LG's AI data center cooling business draws on six decades of HVAC engineering experience in high-reliability environments such as nuclear power plants and large hospitals. Building on recent successes in supplying cooling solutions to hyperscale AI data centers in North America, LG is also expanding its global footprint with key data center projects in the Middle East and Indonesia. By leveraging the integrated capabilities of the broader LG Group to offer comprehensive cooling solutions, the company aims to drive mid- to long-term revenue growth. The global AI data center market presents significant growth opportunities. According to Fortune Business Insights, the market is expected to grow by approximately 26 percent annually, reaching $133.5 billion by 2034. In its second-quarter 2026 earnings report, LG highlighted that first-half orders for data center cooling solutions exceeded $428 million, and the company expects orders to reach several billion dollars by year-end. The company expects to achieve its 2027 chiller business revenue target of approximately $680 million (1 trillion Korean won) ahead of schedule.2 Leveraging Complementary Capabilities to Address Exploding Demand "This agreement reflects the confidence data center customers place in AIR to deliver mission-critical infrastructure at a scale and pace the industry has never seen before," said Brad Hobbs, Chief Executive Officer of AIR Control Concepts. "LG's high-efficiency chiller technology gives us a proven platform we can deploy with confidence across our AI data center portfolio, and this agreement positions AIR to support our customers' growth for years to come." "As heat management in AI data centers emerges as a major global priority, LG aims to be a major player in the global AIDC cooling market," said James Lee, president of the LG Electronics ES Company. "We will achieve this through our differentiated technology, including our high-efficiency chillers, and our rapidly expanding experience in supplying leading big tech companies." "We're excited to deepen our partnership with LG at exactly the moment our industry needs it most," said Hayden Bland, President of AIR Control Concepts. "Data center operators are looking for partners who can deliver mission-critical reliability, capacity and certainty at scale. Together with LG, we're building the technology, manufacturing capacity and support infrastructure to meet that need. For data center customers planning their next generation of infrastructure, now is the time to engage with us." "Data center cooling represents a key pillar of LG's global growth strategy, and this major supply agreement with AIR marks an inflection point for LG's North American chiller business," said Don Kwack, CEO, LG Electronics North America. "This alliance leverages LG's proven cooling innovations and AIR's strong position with U.S. data center developers at a critical time for reliable AI infrastructure expansion." 1 Based on LG's internal simulation of a single 1,750 kW unit operating at 100 percent cooling capacity under climate conditions in the Seoul metropolitan area. Annual energy consumption was calculated at 1,479,655 kWh

The company bid in partnership with Madhav Infra Projects Ltd, which emerged as the L1 bidder for Cluster C of UPCL's tender under the tariff-based competitive bidding mechanism, JWL said in a statement. The projects involve supply and commissioning of BESS systems worth about ₹100 crore. The project was secured in August 2026. Substation-level storage of the kind being deployed in Uttarakhand and West Bengal is central to the framework, and JEM Energy is building its utility-scale portfolio in line with it, it added. "Winning the Uttarakhand project and receiving the formal award for Jeerat are important steps in building JEM Energy into a scalable energy storage business," JWL Managing Director Vivek Lohia said. The company reiterated its target of building a BESS order book of about ₹1,000 crore by FY27. "As the business scales, we expect Jupiter Electric Mobility (JEM) to turn EBITDA positive in Q3 FY27 and to turn profitable by FY28. We will continue to bid with discipline for utility-scale and Commercial & Industrial (C&I) opportunities across India," Lohia said.

artigo.texto: TONGANOXIE, Kan. — — About 150 people gathered in Tonganoxie Sunday with a unified message: responsible AI development matters. Watch Ryan's 5 p.m. report in the video player below. The community turned out to hear the latest on Project Bluestem, a proposed 1,000-acre hyperscale data center campus paired with a gas power plant, as residents continue to push back against a project they say has no place in their community. "These corporations don't care about you," Matt Beat, aka "Mr. Beat," the keynote speaker, influencer, and YouTuber, told listeners. The feeling is mutual in Tonganoxie. KSHB 41 News Reporter Ryan Gamboa recently covered a special meeting with Leavenworth County commissioners, where commissioners Dove and Smith were absent. In the meeting, more than 1,000 neighbors argued why Project Bluestem doesn't belong in their community. Tyler Romans, a Tonganoxie resident, says the fight reflects something far deeper than a land use dispute. "Tonganoxie and the fight against this data center is really a microcosm for the broader issues in American politics," Romans said. "We are David fighting Goliath. And Goliath has a million dollars and two million lawyers, and we're over here trying to scrape by." Tensions continue to flare in Leavenworth County over the county government's inaction on the Project Bluestem data center project. Romans told Gamboa he's frustrated that elected leaders are advocating for these projects. At the state level, he placed blame on state lawmakers for passing Senate Bill 98, which is home to tax breaks and data center developers. "The failure of that state and county government and local government to protect us. We elected these people to guide our communities into prosperity, but there is no guidance. It's a sellout," Romans said. The political stakes sharpened last week when the Leavenworth County Commission voted 3-to-2 to remove Mike Stieben as commissioner chair. The title is merely ceremonial. But it comes with a responsibility. Commissioner Jeff Culbertson moved to make the change during the meeting. "I'd like to bring up something that I've been asked to do for months... take a vote of the board on changing out the chair, " Jeff Culbertson, a Leavenworth County commissioner, brought up during the Sept. 30 meeting. Stieben has been a vocal opponent of the data center project, along with his constituents. Commissioners Culbertson, Dove, and Reid pointed out Stieben's actions are the cause. "It's the Mike Stieben show," Reid pointed out. Stieben pushed back on the commissioners' motion to oust him, claiming the motivation stems from them wanting to approve the data center development. "You're going to saddle Tonganoxie with this project. That's what this is completely about," Commissioner Stieben said on Wednesday. Stieben told Gamboa on Sunday that the removal won't silence him and it may have backfired. "It was an attempt to silence me, but um not gonna be silenced, I'm not gonna be silenced. I represent Tonganoxie, I represent Linwood, we're gonna continue to represent them," Stieben said. "There's a lot more freedom not being the Chair, and maybe they should've considered that because my entire focus until January is to focus on this project for my constituents." For Romans, the political fallout is a call to action at the ballot box. "When we see our leadership fail us, that is when we need to start talking about voting these people out. That was a huge primary driver in the primaries that just happened, and it's going to be a huge driver in the elections in November," Romans said. Rebecca Davis, organizer for the Tongie Data Center Watchdog, says the movement is gaining ground. "Definitely the resistance is growing. 7 out of 10 Americans don't want a data center in their community. That lines up pretty good here in Tonganoxie," Davis explained. Davis added that the data center debate needs to go deeper than economics. "What is AI? How can it ethically fit into our society? I think it has great benefits in the medical field, but we don't need AI slop taking over everything," Davis said. "We don't need mass loss of jobs. So, ethical AI is amazing, but hitting the gas on hyper-scale data centers, just do it as fast as you can, just no." For Romans, the stakes of the movement dying couldn't be higher, and more personal. "We keep fighting because there is no plan B for us, because we're going to live here no matter what. I would much rather live in the town I fell in love with than an industrial hellscape," Romans said. Commissioner Stieben still has no doubt how it's all going to end. "I believe we're going to win this," Stieben said. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy. —

Dear Bess, ADHD didn’t exist when I was younger. Now all three of my grandkids have been diagnosed with it. I’m not even sure I believe it’s real. How do I deal with this as a grandmother? Signed, Sceptical Nan Sceptical Nan, I want to start by taking your observation seriously, because I think it’s more reasonable than you’ve perhaps been given credit for. You’re right that almost nobody was being diagnosed with ADHD when you were raising your own children. That’s not a false memory. It’s a genuine, well-documented fact. So let’s separate two things, because I think they’ve become tangled together in your mind, understandably. The first is whether ADHD, as a real, biological difference in how a brain works, actually exists. The second is why so many more children are being diagnosed with it now than in your day. Those are genuinely different questions, and I think the honest answer to the second one is actually what’s fuelling your doubt about the first. Here’s what the research genuinely shows. ADHD is one of the most heritable conditions in psychiatry, with studies putting the genetic contribution at around 80 per cent. Twin studies have found identical twins share an ADHD diagnosis around 81 per cent of the time, compared to just 29 per cent for fraternal twins, which is about as strong a signal of a real, biological basis as you’ll find for almost any condition. Researchers have also identified specific genes involved in dopamine regulation that show up consistently in people with ADHD. This isn’t a fashionable label invented to explain away ordinary childhood behaviour. It’s a genuine, inherited difference in brain function, sitting alongside things like eye colour or a family tendency toward migraines, mostly out of anyone’s control. What has genuinely changed is who gets identified. The diagnostic criteria themselves have been broadened more than once, most notably in 1994 and again in 2013, when the age by which symptoms needed to first appear was pushed out from seven to twelve. Awareness among doctors, teachers and parents has grown enormously. And it’s now well understood that girls and quieter, less disruptive children were routinely missed for decades, because the original picture of ADHD was built almost entirely around loud, hyperactive little boys. A very recent Danish study of more than two million children, published just this week, found that children diagnosed with ADHD today actually resemble the general population more closely than those diagnosed a decade ago, suggesting the diagnostic net has genuinely widened to catch milder, previously overlooked presentations, not that the condition has been invented from nothing. So my honest answer, Nan, is this: the condition was almost certainly always there. What’s changed is that we’ve finally built the tools, and the willingness, to actually see it. Now, the more important question. What do you actually do with this, as a grandmother? Here’s where I’d gently steer you. Your grandchildren’s parents have presumably gone through a genuine, often lengthy assessment process to arrive at three separate diagnoses. That’s not something families pursue lightly, and it’s worth trusting that process, even if the framework itself is unfamiliar to you. Your scepticism, if it’s shared openly with your grandchildren or spoken about within earshot, risks landing as a quiet message that their diagnosis, and by extension, their struggles, aren’t real or aren’t taken seriously. That’s a genuinely painful thing for a child to absorb from someone they love, even unintentionally. What I’d suggest instead is holding your questions privately, or raising them directly and respectfully with their parents, rather than with the children themselves. Ask what you can do to support them, practically, day to day. Ask what helps and what doesn’t. You don’t need to fully understand the science to be a genuinely steady, loving presence in their lives, and honestly, that steadiness matters far more to a child than whether their grandmother has fully come around on the diagnostic criteria. One last thought, Sceptical Nan. You raised children in a world that simply didn’t have this language yet. That’s not a failing on your part, and it doesn’t make your instincts wrong to question something new. But I’d encourage you to let your genuine curiosity lead here, rather than your doubt. Ask questions. Read a little. You may find, as so many grandparents eventually do, that what you’re really looking at isn’t something new at all, just something that finally has a name. Have a question for Bess? Write to her at community@startsat60.com with “Dear Bess” in the subject line. Join the conversation. Comments are reviewed before they appear. Partilhar Duas metodologias, centradas na Reflorestação e na Gestão Florestal Melhorada, foram lançadas pelo executivo. Mais projetos podem surgir, permitindo a redução de emissões carbónicas. O Mercado Voluntário de Carbono (MVC) passa a contar com três metodologias, em Portugal. O objetivo passa por reduzir as emissões carbónicas para a atmosfera, por forma a gerar créditos de carbono. Por decisão do Ministério do Ambiente e Energia, foram aprovadas duas novas metodologias de carbono dedicadas à Reflorestação e à Gestão Florestal Melhorada, que se juntam à já existente metodologia para Novas Florestações. A medida foi transmitida num comunicado enviado às redações. Na mira está o aumento das oportunidades para desenvolvimento de projetos de sequestro de carbono em território nacional e para a captação de investimento privado. Em causa está a geração de um crédito por cada tonelada de CO2 poupada em emissões. Posteriormente, os créditos podem ser vendidos a empresas que queiram libertar carbono para a atmosfera. “Estamos a criar condições para que mais proprietários, entidades e empresas possam investir na floresta e na ação climática", salienta a ministra do Ambiente e da Energia, Maria da Graça Carvalho. O alargamento das metodologias disponíveis permite reforçar "a credibilidade e a capacidade de crescimento do MVC", assim como incentivar ao "financiamento privado para projetos que contribuem simultaneamente para a neutralidade carbónica, valorização do território e resiliência das nossas florestas”, aponta. O MVC conta, à data, com dois projetos registados na metodologia Novas Florestações e um terceiro que aguarda validação inicial. Estão disponíveis para venda 977 créditos de carbono. Para tal, o Portal do Mercado Voluntário de Carbono conta com 29 utilizadores registados, ao mesmo tempo que existem 10 verificadores qualificados para assegurar a validação inicial e a verificação periódica dos projetos, informa o Ministério.

artigo.texto: Mount Pleasant committee revisits data center issues as moratorium advances MOUNT PLEASANT, S.C. (WCIV) — The Mount Pleasant Planning Committee plans to take another look at data center development at a Monday meeting, after steps were taken toward enacting a pause on new data center projects. According to the committee, Monday night's meeting will look at zoning rules and land use as the town continues to push toward a 120 day pause on new proposed data center projects. If the council approves the moratorium, leaders would be allowed more time to define what qualifies as a data center and create a public review process so that residents can have input on data center projects. There are reportedly no current large-scale data center proposals, however this meeting and the 120 day pause aims to help the committee put rules in place to help guide future projects before they are proposed. The committee will meet at 1:15 p.m. on Oct. 5.

artigo.texto: Adaptogen Capital, a specialist investment firm at the forefront of the energy transition, is pleased to announce the next phase of its European growth strategy, as it targets €1bn of investment opportunities by 2030 across European Battery Energy Storage (BESS) markets. Highlights: - Adaptogen has developed a 1.2GW pipeline of Belgian BESS opportunities, with five initial projects in development and progressing towards final investment decision (FID). - Adaptogen has also progressed a further 500MW portfolio in Germany across two sites at key offshore wind HV landing points on the transmission grid. - Adaptogen’s first fund, closed in 2023, has now been fully committed to the development and operation of UK BESS assets through its operating platform Varco Energy, with a follow on co-investment raise in 2025. - Adaptogen is now exploring capital raising in 2027 to assist in funding its initial European BESS assets, with a likely requirement of €260m equity and €500m of debt. Adaptogen Capital today sets out its continued expansion into continental Europe, having built a pipeline of Belgian opportunities through its operating platform MVA Energy, that address grid congestion and the integration of growing renewable generation, alongside a parallel German pipeline. The firm’s approach is structured around project-specific capital commitments at FID, allowing infrastructure investors the opportunity to back firm connection projects with low grid fees once development and permitting risk has been substantially reduced. Investor appetite for European battery energy storage is strengthening as power market volatility, geopolitical and inflation concerns, rising renewable penetration and growing grid constraints reinforce the role of storage as critical energy infrastructure. With relatively few specialist BESS managers operating at scale across the region, Adaptogen believes its project-led approach is well aligned with the needs of infrastructure investors seeking exposure to the central asset class in the next phase of the energy transition. Adaptogen’s European ambitions build directly on its UK experience. The firm’s original fund closed in 2023 and has since been fully deployed to develop, construct and operate grid-scale BESS assets through its Varco Energy platform, with 350MW on track to be operational by 2028 and a further 275MW in development. Battery energy storage is increasingly recognised across Europe as critical infrastructure for balancing intermittent renewable generation and easing grid congestion. Adaptogen’s disciplined, project-led approach to capital deployment is intended to support that transition as it extends its strategy beyond the UK. James Mills, Managing Director, Adaptogen Capital, commented: “Across Europe, grids are under growing pressure from the pace of renewable build-out, and that is creating a clear investment case for well-located, grid scale battery storage with firm connections, backed by sensibly structured revenue and debt facilities. We have spent the past three years building a pipeline that targets that opportunity, and our approach of committing capital once projects have reached final investment decision allows infrastructure investors to back assets where development risk has already been substantially reduced. Our experience delivering and operating storage assets in the UK through Varco Energy gives us a strong foundation as we extend that model into continental Europe.” Building, Design & Construction Magazine | The Choice of Industry Professionals

artigo.texto: BYD's Xixian Battery Plant Hits Full Throttle as Washington Delays Connected-Vehicle Ban Published on 10/04/2026 at 13:51 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD's newest battery cell facility in Xixian, Shaanxi province, has reached full production, the company's Yicai-reported milestone arriving just as its shares came under pressure from a global bond-market selloff. The plant, built at a cost of 7 billion CNY, carries an annual capacity of 16 gigawatt-hours and ranks among the first sites manufacturing BYD's second-generation Blade battery. Bringing cell production in-house is central to the automaker's strategy of keeping manufacturing costs in check. That operational progress, announced Wednesday, stood in contrast to the stock's performance. BYD shares finished Friday at 8.39 EUR on European trading venues, down 2.4% on the day, as surging US Treasury yields triggered a broad retreat across Asian equity markets. Several Chinese electric-vehicle makers, Li Auto and XPeng among them, fell in sympathy, though Geely managed to buck the trend. JPMorgan Cuts Its Rating Market sentiment was further dented by JPMorgan, which downgraded BYD from Overweight to Neutral and slashed its price target to 88 HKD from 124 HKD. The brokerage pointed to lackluster domestic demand, rising input costs, and persistent trade-policy and regulatory uncertainty facing Chinese carmakers. The downgrade was reported Wednesday, with some accounts placing the move a day earlier. The cautious stance reflects a home market where consumers remain on the sidelines. According to Reuters, BYD continues to grapple with weak demand in China, where a bruising price war has made buyers hesitant. Investors in Hong Kong responded tepidly to the company's latest disclosures, with the local listing slipping after trading resumed Friday. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Exports Do the Heavy Lifting September delivery figures, released Thursday, laid bare the split between home and abroad. Total vehicle sales climbed 17% year over year to 463,561 units, but the expansion was powered overwhelmingly by overseas markets: exports of passenger cars and pickups outside China jumped 153.9% to 179,877 units. Those booming shipments are doing much of the work of offsetting the sluggish domestic picture. The overseas push, however, cuts both ways. It opens fresh sales channels while drawing Chinese manufacturers deeper into the crosshairs of foreign regulators and trade officials. A Reprieve in Washington On that front, the US Senate on Wednesday postponed deliberations on a bill that would permanently bar the import, production, and sale of connected vehicles and related hardware and software with Chinese links. The delay hands Chinese automakers, BYD included, a temporary breather from looming restrictions on access to the North American market. For the year to date, unaudited company figures show total sales of 3,131,576 vehicles across the first nine months, a decline of 3.94% compared with the same period a year earlier. After the recent losses, the stock trades 4.5% above its 52-week low. The picture for investors is one of a company pulled in two directions: an overseas expansion that is generating real momentum, set against trade-policy decisions in Washington and elsewhere that remain a significant wildcard for the business ahead. artigo.texto: Vista aérea de um data center da AWS que integra a região US-EAST-1, no norte da Virgínia, nos EUA — Foto: Reuters/Jonathan Ernst Incentivos fiscais, fabricação local de componentes e IA brasileira: os candidatos à Presidência mais bem colocados nas pesquisas apresentam essas como algumas das propostas em seus planos de governo para atrair a construção de data centers no Brasil. ❓ Um data center ("centro de dados", em inglês) é um local que armazena e processa informações. Entre os modelos mais comuns, estão os de nuvem — cloud, para armazenar arquivos e operar serviços na internet — e de inteligência artificial, para treinar modelos de linguagem complexos. Facilitar a construção de data centers é uma ação que alguns dos candidatos consideram importante para aproveitar o avanço da IA. Mas, enquanto o Brasil tenta atrair essas instalações, países como os Estados Unidos têm enfrentado protestos contra o avanço do setor. Com rejeição em outros lugares, por que candidatos no Brasil querem atrair mais data centers? Entre os motivos, estão as diferenças no tamanho dos mercados e nas matrizes energéticas dos países. Os EUA têm mais de 4.700 data centers e lideram o segmento, segundo dados de setembro do site Data Center Map. O Brasil, por sua vez, tem 218 complexos desse tipo e ocupa o 12º lugar no ranking. Com menos instalações, é preciso armazenar e processar muitos dados no exterior: o Brasil terminou 2025 com déficit de US$ 8 bilhões na balança comercial de Serviços de Computação e Informação, segundo a Brasscom, associação de empresas brasileiras de tecnologia. E, enquanto os EUA dependem principalmente de energia gerada por combustíveis fósseis, incluindo petróleo e gás natural, a eletricidade no Brasil é gerada em larga escala por fontes renováveis, como usinas hidrelétricas. O que há de comum no Brasil, nos EUA e em outros países é a discussão sobre o consumo elevado de energia e água por data centers: moradores de várias cidades americanas protestaram contra o avanço dessas instalações, e autoridades brasileiras questionaram os impactos desses projetos. Para Daniel Cordeiro, professor na Universidade de São Paulo (USP) e especialista em computação sustentável e de alto desempenho, o Brasil precisa aumentar sua capacidade computacional, mas deve tentar evitar problemas que estão sendo enfrentados em outros países. "Ainda não chegamos na quantidade de data centers e de problemas que esses outros países já têm. Temos que olhar para os problemas que estão acontecendo nos outros países e nos precaver para que o mesmo não aconteça aqui", diz. Segundo Thais Ortega, coordenadora de pesquisa da consultoria Reglab, a atração de data centers é um consenso entre os principais candidatos, mas há diferenças nos modelos previstos para alcançar esse objetivo. "Todos convergem para atrair, mas como será a atração? O Brasil tem uma posição estratégica, com vários pontos positivos. Não temos como prever se teremos ou não os problemas dos EUA, mas temos como tentar mitigar com regulações", destaca. Marina Garrote, diretora de operações do Reglab, diz que o Redata, regime brasileiro que reduz impostos para data centers, mas exige contrapartidas socioambientais, pode fazer o país superar alguns dos desafios enfrentados nos EUA. "Com a matriz energética dos EUA, mais data centers significam mais emissões de carbono e conta de luz mais alta para o vizinho. No Brasil, se a expansão for, de fato, baseada em energia eólica e solar, o custo social será um pouco diferente", afirma. Rejeição americana Protesto em Frederick, Maryland, contra a expansão de data centers — Foto: Elizabeth Bauer Nos EUA, 64% da população discorda da ideia de que construir data centers rapidamente será positivo para o país, revelou uma pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos. O levantamento indicou que 57% são contrários à criação desses complexos em seus bairros. Mesmo com a forte rejeição, o presidente Donald Trump tem defendido o avanço das instalações. Em encontro com executivos de gigantes de tecnologia na última terça-feira (29), ele afirmou que esses empreendimentos serão muito populares no país. Entre os convidados, estavam Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg e Sundar Pichai, líderes da xAI, da Meta e do Google, empresas que desenvolvem modelos de inteligência artificial, além de Jensen Huang, da Nvidia, principal fabricante de chips para treinamento de IA. O encontro terminou com um compromisso das empresas para reforçar controles de segurança de seus modelos de IA após episódios em que eles saíram do controle e fizeram ataques cibernéticos. Trump disse que as companhias "querem fazer o que é certo" e vão se "autorregular". "Essas empresas grandes, poderosas, muito ricas e inteligentes farão contribuições enormes para as comunidades", disse Trump sobre os data centers. "Farão coisas realmente benéficas, tanto financeiramente quanto de outras formas". Renúncia fiscal no Brasil O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) sancionou em setembro o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Data Center (Redata), que zera impostos de importação de equipamentos usados nos data centers. Para aproveitar o benefício, as empresas deverão usar apenas energia renovável ou de baixo carbono e gastar, no máximo, 50ml de água por quilowatt-hora (kWh). Elas também deverão destinar 10% da capacidade para o mercado brasileiro e 2% do valor dos equipamentos em pesquisa no país. artigo.texto: [ESPAÑOL ABAJO | PORTUGUÊS ABAIXO] Colombia’s new government will initiate proceedings to lift a 50% cap on carbon credit retirements against CO2 tax liabilities – handing a win to voluntary carbon market (VCM) sellers, and boosting the significance of compliance measures in response to trade pressures from the EU. Minister of Environment and Sustainable Development Fabio Arjona announced in Medellin that the new government of right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella would propose the change to Congress. Latin American and Caribbean countries enjoy relatively low trade exposure to the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which prices in the embedded carbon of goods entering the bloc. Still, Colombia ranks just behind Brazil as the most EU CBAM-exposed Latin American or Caribbean countries. Colombia’s COP 29,070.49 ($8.76) per tonne CO2 tax rate may alleviate some of the border carbon burden by creating an EU-recognised domestic carbon price that’s deductible from CBAM fees. In its current form, the European Commission’s draft implementing act would make the price paid for carbon credits retired under the tax eligible for deductions, too – enhancing the role of the VCM to address both domestic and international carbon pricing compliance. Arjona simultaneously announced the revocation of Ministerial Decree 0973 on the VCM, which established restrictions in line with former President Gustavo Petro’s criticisms of the market and was published in early August. EMISSIONS TRADING SYSTEMS Both Colombia and Brazil are working to implement emissions trading systems – called the ‘PNCTE’ in Colombia, and the ‘SBCE’ in Brazil. These schemes could also create EU-recognised carbon prices. In Brazil, carbon project co-developer Earthshot Labs Brazil has seen some foreign investors take a cautious approach due to uncertainty in the SBCE’s final design, Carbon Pulse reported last week. That does not mean that investment in the Brazilian VCM has halted, according to the co-developer’s director Rita Croce – rather, some investors are holding out for projects that could potentially generate Article 6 Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs) in the future. Brazil’s increasingly crowded carbon asset ecosystem would include SBCE allowances, called CBEs; SBCE-eligible voluntary carbon credits, called CRVEs; voluntary credits bearing a Letter of Authorisation; and regular voluntary units. Purchasing either CBEs or CRVEs for use in the SBCE could potentially fall under the European Commission’s draft vision for a ‘carbon price effectively paid’ in a third country, for CBAM purposes. Meanwhile, Colombia’s Ministerial Decree 0969 from the now-departed Petro administration stated that up to 3.3% of PNCTE compliance units could be sourced from the VCM – a far lower percentage than what was initially pitched in a Sep. 2024 consultation document. The fate of the PNCTE under De La Espriella is unclear. J-REDD+ QUESTIONS Meanwhile, a Brazilian state and Argentine province grappled with thorny implementation questions for jurisdictional REDD+ (J-REDD+). A proposed road in the Amazon could result in up to 133,800 hectares of additional deforestation over 20 years – putting Brazilian state Acre’s J-REDD+ goals at risk, according to a report published by NGOs Amazon Conservation and SOS Amazonia. Acre’s J-REDD+ programme is registered under the ART standard’s TREES protocol. Researchers noted that the modelling is not meant to predict actual future losses, but that plans for new road developments placed Acre at “a critical juncture”. In Argentina, senators for the province of Misiones – itself promoting a large-scale, Verra-registered J-REDD+ programme – are mounting partial opposition to a national bill they helped draft. Senator Sonia Rojas Decut has taken issue with the bill’s definition of ‘project owner’ (Spanish: titular del proyecto). The definition would effectively require written consent from thousands of native forest owners to implement programmes at the provincial level, she argued. The bill would therefore “make it impossible for Argentine provinces to implement jurisdictional programmes”, she wrote. Argentine media has reported that while the bill disappeared from the agenda for last week’s Senate session, members of ruling party La Libertad Avanza have indicated that they will participate in ongoing negotiations with Misiones in hopes of bringing the bill to a future session. artigo.texto: KALAMAZOO, MI (WKZO AM/FM) – It has been one of the least controversial issues the Kalamazoo city commission has had to deal with this year, but one of the most emotional. Opinions have been nearly unanimous that the city needs to brace itself, and thoroughly prepare for the day someone wants to build a data center, or any other potentially worrisome high-tech facility in town. They have scheduled a final public hearing and a vote this evening. Kalamazoo city commissioners are set to finalize a one year moratorium, to buy time to redraft zoning codes to make sure if a data center or large battery energy storage system is proposed, that it won’t become a problem for its neighbors or the community. Assistant City Planner Bobby Durkee says that one year clock begins with tonight’s approval. “The goal of the moratorium is to develop those zoning standards and appropriate land uses, and to study for a transparent public process. For staff in the community to research the topic, understand the topic and draft regulations because you cannot outright ban a use.” He says as recommended by the planning commission, staff will set up a working group to assist in the research. “You know I look at things like public utilities, private utilities, residents, neighborhoods, the industry itself.” Several commissioners implored him not to make it top-heavy with industry and utility experts and to make sure it represents community and environmental interests too. Commissioner Chris Praedel says it’s “so critically important that there are people sitting in those seats that are just everyday people, you know, that care a lot about this issue.” While communities have some flexibility in how it sets up its own zoning regulations, it’s still a process that is guided by state laws and technical requirements and must be detailed and specific if a community wants to avoid legal challenges, or leave gaps or loopholes. Data centers have become a major state and national issue this election year with national polls showing 65 to 70% of the public opposed to having a data center in their community and only 20% supporting. The numbers are even higher for Democratic and younger voters.

A 2000 study called “Trading is Hazardous to Your Wealth: The Common Stock Investment Performance of Individual Investors” evaluated 66,465 U.S. households that held stocks from 1991 to 1996. The households that traded most averaged an 11.4% annual return during a period where the overall market gained 17.9%. These lower returns were attributed to overconfidence. A 2014 paper (revised 2019) titled “Learning Fast or Slow?” analyzed the complete transaction history of the Taiwan Stock Exchange between 1992 and 2006. It looked at the ongoing performance of day traders in this sample, and found that 97% of day traders can expect to lose money from trading, and more than 90% of all day trading volume can be traced to investors who predictably lose money. Additionally, it tied the behavior of gamblers and drivers who get more speeding tickets to overtrading, and cited studies showing that legalized gambling has an inverse effect on trading volume. A 2019 research study (revised 2020) called “Day Trading for a Living?” observed 19,646 Brazilian futures contract traders who started day trading from 2013 to 2015, and recorded two years of their trading activity. The study authors found that 97% of traders with more than 300 days actively trading lost money, and only 1.1% earned more than the Brazilian minimum wage ($16 USD per day). They hypothesized that the greater returns shown in previous studies did not differentiate between frequent day traders and those who traded rarely, and that more frequent trading activity decreases the chance of profitability. These studies show the wide variance of the available data on day trading profitability. One thing that seems clear from the research is that most day traders lose money . artigo.texto: UAE-based real assets investor and developer ROX Capital Group has launched the ROX Gulf Energy Storage Platform, targeting utility-scale and commercial energy storage projects in the UAE and Oman while exploring opportunities for regional assembly and manufacturing. The platform will evaluate a range of storage technologies, including vanadium redox flow, lithium iron phosphate and sodium-ion batteries, as well as long-duration solutions such as CO₂ batteries, gravity-based storage, compressed-air energy storage and thermal storage. ROX plans to establish partnerships with selected technology providers based on their track record in deploying large-scale storage projects, long-duration storage expertise where applicable, financial and operational capacity, and ownership or control of core technology intellectual property. The company said it will prioritise providers with bankable systems, established manufacturing capabilities and the ability to offer long-term technical support, performance guarantees and warranties. The platform and its partners will pursue upcoming energy storage tenders and assess local assembly or manufacturing opportunities where commercially viable. “The Gulf is building some of the world’s largest solar projects. The next challenge is ensuring that clean power remains available after sunset and during periods of peak demand,” said Robin Antony, Founder of ROX Capital Group. “No single technology will meet every requirement. We are building a platform that matches the right technology to the needs of each project and, where viable, supports the development of local manufacturing capability.” “Lithium-ion batteries have transformed energy storage and will remain an important part of the solution,” Antony added. “However, the Gulf’s climate, load profile and energy-security priorities create a need for a broader portfolio of technologies. High summer temperatures can increase cooling requirements, while solar-heavy systems require storage over longer periods after dark. We see an important role for technologies including vanadium flow batteries, CO₂ batteries, gravity-based storage and thermal storage alongside lithium-ion solutions.” -TradeArabia News Service

artigo.texto: As if Emporia’s data center debate needed any more controversy. With the general election essentially a month away, Emporians for Progress spokesman Casey Woods says the ordinance language behind the petitions hoping to ban data centers and battery energy storage systems don’t reference city Planning and Zoning regulations currently on the books. The petitions reference Article 15, but Planning and Zoning code uses Sections instead of Articles and only goes up to Section 12. Emporia Neighbors United founder Jay Vehige sees things differently, although he admits there was a “drafting error” before the petition was turned in. The original petition and ordinance were submitted July 14, according to City Manager Trey Cocking. It was certified by the Lyon County Clerk’s Office on July 21 and was passed by the Emporia City Commission on August 5. Cocking says Vehige tried to submit revised petitions August 7, but he tells KVOE News cities have no ability to alter what was originally submitted — meaning residents have to vote on the original package due to KSA 12-3013. This is the second clerical or drafting error in this petition process for Emporia Neighbors United. The original petitions submitted were invalidated because petition circulators didn’t verify they witnessed petitions being signed. Vehige has told KVOE News that issue was due to a paperwork error in attaching circulator forms to signature petition forms. Woods says Emporians for Progress sees this as one reason to oppose the ballot questions. Vehige counters Woods’ assertions, saying his guidance indicates the Article 15 reference would not invalidate both petitions in their entirety. Vehige also says he has spoken with City Attorney Christina Montgomery, who was out of the office last week and is currently unavailable for an interview. Cocking sent a statement to KVOE News. saying the Article 15 reference will be one issue to be addressed by the court for effect and “enforceability.” He also says the city is not speculating how this will be addressed in court with that process a distinct possibility. Woods sees potential lawsuits throughout the 10-year halt if the questions are approved. The city has asked for rulings on whether the petitions are legislative or administrative in nature. Administrative rulings would likely invalidate the petitions — and, if the petitions are approved but Kansas Senior Judge Glenn Braun rules the petitions are administrative after the Nov. 3 general election, the vote results would be invalidated as well. Vehige believes Judge Braun will side with Emporia Neighbors United. There is no date for when Judge Braun will rule on the nature of the 2 ballot questions. This continues a busy time for news when it comes to data centers locally. A lawsuit filed by Emporia City Commissioner Erren Harter against Recall Committee members Haley Bradford, Kathleen Lamb and Vehige — also including Lyon County Legal Counsel Molly Priest and County Clerk Amie Jones as defendants — ended Thursday with an “agreed upon order” that essentially says this version of a recall petition cannot move forward under any circumstances. Priest and the case paperwork say this does not stop future petitions seeking Harter’s recall cannot move forward. A grand jury determining whether Harter conducted misconduct in office will be empaneled Monday. Meanwhile, Amanda Mendoza, Kenneth Bruner, Ann Bruner and the separate Bruner trusts have filed a lawsuit against the city of Emporia, alleging the zoning part of the Digital Infrastructure overlay was not properly handled. The lawsuit, LY-2026-CV-124, says the Emporia Planning Commission did not have either the jurisdiction or the authorization to review applications for zoning classifications that did not exist when applications were filed — meaning, according to the lawsuit, the city’s decision to approve the overlay was unlawful and the subsequent rezoning of 11 tracts of land was unauthorized and without proper jurisdiction. On top of that, Vehige says Emporia Neighbors United will push to bring 2 more petitions to the ballot by early next year. One would change the form of city government from its current at-large City Commission structure to a 4-ward City Council system with one at-large position. The other would change the method of filling unexpired City Commission or City Council positions from appointment to public vote. In separate news related to the Emporia data center project, the Flint Hills Digital Campus website is no longer public-facing. The website went public in early June as the data center project was announced. Project spokesman Garrett Nordstrom says flinthillsdigitalcampus.com was meant to be an informational site before rezoning and was meant to “dispel misconceptions.” Nordstrom says the website still exists but is internal now and is being shared with potential end users. Nordstrom says no end user has been selected for the proposed data center in west Emporia. He also says it would be unusual for a public website to document a private development project. The data center ballot questions will be part of KVOE’s political interviews later this month ahead of the general election Nov. 3. Appearing at 10:06 am Oct. 20 will be Vehige and Edgar Esparza from Emporia Neighbors United, as well as Woods representing Emporians for Progress. Our remaining interview slate is as follows: *Tuesday: Candidate Profile with Kansas House 13th District challenger Democrat Mark Remmert. Incumbent Republican Duane Droge did not confirm interest in a forum-style interview *Thursday: Candidate Forum with Kansas House 60th District challenger Democrat Maddison Glover and incumbent Republican Mark Schreiber *Oct 13: Candidate Forum with Kansas House 76th District nominees Democrat David Claridge and Republican Russel Stukey Click here for the KVOE Voter Information Guide courtesy Community National Bank & Trust.
