artigo.texto: Since the Iran-US military conflict began earlier this year, disrupting global oil markets, Australia’s electric vehicle (EV) market has experienced an unprecedented boost. With motorists facing sharp increases at the bowser and continuing uncertainty about fuel prices, many drivers have decided to go electric. EVs accounted for 25.8% of total car sales in the first half of 2026. One brand in particular is capitalising on this trend, and that’s the Chinese carmaker BYD, whose name was previously spelled out as “Build Your Dreams”. It is now outselling many far older and more established competitors in Australia. Fifteen years ago, Elon Musk poked fun at BYD, saying it was not a serious competitor in the electric vehicle business. And until just a few years ago, hardly anyone in Australia had even heard of the brand. So how did BYD become such a formidable competitor in the EV market so quickly? BYD’s origin story BYD’s story began not with cars, but batteries. In 1995, 29-year-old battery specialist Wang Chuanfu founded the company in Shenzhen with a small team. BYD initially manufactured rechargeable nickel-cadmium batteries, before moving into lithium-ion batteries. The company grew quickly, and by 2000, BYD had become Motorola’s first Chinese supplier of lithium-ion batteries. Nokia followed in 2002, and the same year BYD listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. In 2003, BYD entered the automotive industry by acquiring a struggling Chinese manufacturer. Its first model, the petrol-powered F3, arrived in 2005. By then, BYD was already looking towards electrification. In 2008, it launched the F3DM plug-in hybrid. That same year, legendary US investor Warren Buffett backed the company with an investment of about US$230 million for a 9.9% stake, which he later sold. When Bloomberg asked Tesla chief executive Elon Musk in 2011 about BYD as a potential competitor, he laughed. “Have you seen their car?” he asked, before saying he did not see BYD as a competitor. But, by 2023, his assessment had completely changed: “Their cars are highly competitive these days.” What do the sales numbers say these days? Sales figures both in Australia and overseas show just how rapidly BYD has become a formidable name in the automotive industry. Globally, BYD went from selling about 190,000 battery or hybrid vehicles in 2020 to 4.6 million in 2025 – a roughly 24-fold increase in just five years. Of the 2025 sales, 2.26 million were fully electric, enough to overtake Tesla’s 1.64 million deliveries. Its rise in Australia has been similarly striking. In the first eight months of 2026, BYD sold more than 68,000 vehicles, making it Australia’s second-highest-selling car brand behind Toyota. In the month of June, just 243 sales separated the two. Among electric vehicles, over the same period, BYD sold more than 39,000 cars, overtaking Tesla to become Australia’s highest-selling electric vehicle brand. What is BYD’s secret sauce? BYD’s rise from a relatively unknown battery maker to a global automotive giant cannot be attributed to any single factor. But four factors have likely been instrumental to its success. First, BYD makes an unusually large proportion of its cars itself. This includes batteries, electric motors, power electronics and even some of the semiconductors its vehicles need. This high degree of “vertical integration” reduces its reliance on outside suppliers and gives BYD greater control over both its supply chain and production costs. The company even owns and operates its own ships to transport the vehicles to Australia and other markets. Second, BYD did not bet everything on fully electric vehicles. It also sells a large range of plug-in hybrids. This gave buyers who are not yet ready to rely entirely on battery power another route into electrification. Third, BYD took a different approach to battery technology. Its Blade Battery uses lithium iron phosphate chemistry, which is generally cheaper than nickel-based alternatives and requires neither nickel nor cobalt. Fourth, BYD has benefited substantially from China’s long-running support for its electric vehicle industry. This has included direct subsidies to manufacturers as well as subsidies and tax incentives for consumers buying electric vehicles. A history of controversy BYD’s rapid expansion has not been without controversy. Despite its global success, BYD has never established passenger-car sales in the United States. More recently, high tariffs and national-security concerns about Chinese vehicles have created prohibitive barriers to entry to the US market. Cybersecurity concerns have also attracted scrutiny in Australia. This was highlighted in a recent ABC Four Corners investigation showing a cybersecurity expert remotely accessing functions in a BYD Shark 6. Safety concerns have emerged too. While safety regulator ANCAP awarded the Shark 6 five stars, it also applied a penalty score for posing a greater risk to oncoming vehicles due to its size, weight and front-end design. The Shark 6 is larger than many of Australia’s largest utes, including some variants of the Ford Ranger. A new global order for autos For decades, Australia’s car market has been dominated by Japanese brands, with US, Korean and European manufacturers also prominent. Chinese brands are now challenging that order remarkably quickly. China made becoming a global leader in electric vehicles an industrial priority. It has largely achieved that ambition. If current momentum continues, the badges Australians see on their roads over the coming decade could look very different from those they grew up with. BYD is one name they are likely to see much more often.

artigo.texto: Hyperscale Data Sets November 12 as Investor Day to Discuss Michigan AI Expansion and Strategic Alternatives Across Its Portfolio Company reiterates 2027 guidance of $300–$350 million in revenue and $60–$80 million in consolidated Adjusted EBITDA LAS VEGAS , Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced that it will virtually host an investor day (the "Investor Day") on November 12, 2026, from 1:15 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. Pacific Time, to discuss the Michigan AI data center campus (the "Michigan Campus"), the status of its other portfolio businesses and strategic alternatives intended to enhance stockholder value. Participation details for Investor Day will be provided at a later date. During the Investor Day, management will provide an update as to the progress on, and expansion of, the Michigan Campus and the executed master services agreement (the "MSA") with a California-based neocloud provider (the "Customer"). As previously disclosed, the MSA contemplates the deployment of an initial 20 megawatts ("MW") of critical AI compute capacity and, if the Customer exercises all of its options to extend the term, and rights to an additional 32 MW of critical AI compute capacity, the MSA could generate more than $3.0 billion in total contract revenue from the potential 52 MW deployment over a 20-year period. The Company has previously announced that it believes the Michigan Campus could ultimately support more than 300 MW of total power capacity. The development of any capacity beyond the initial 20 MW covered by the MSA is subject to financing, regulatory approvals, engineering, utility agreements, infrastructure availability, customer demand and other conditions. There can be no assurance that additional capacity will be developed, financed, contracted or placed into service. Additionally, management is expected to provide a review of the Company's various portfolio businesses within its various sectors, including: defense; energy and infrastructure; hotel operations and commercial real estate holdings; technology and finance; and commercial lending and trading and activist investing. In addition, the Company will be discussing ongoing initiatives, including, without limitation, the AI software platform by the Company's subsidiary askROI, Inc. ("askROI") and blockchain and digital technology initiatives by Ault Markets, Inc., another subsidiary. Management anticipates discussing the Company's evaluation of strategic alternatives, including potentially selling the Michigan Campus, taking public the Company's wholly owned subsidiary, Sentinum, Inc. ("Sentinum") through an initial public offering or the Company's continued ownership and development of the Michigan Campus. The discussion will also address options involving askROI, including a potential sale, strategic partnership or divestiture, and the possibility of combining askROI with a broader technology business. Transactions under evaluation could include equity consideration, which would allow Hyperscale Data to retain an ownership interest in the combined business and participate in its potential upside. "We are focused on delivering the contracted capacity in our Michigan Campus and turning that investment into cash flow," said Milton "Todd" Ault III, Executive Chairman. "Investor Day will also provide an update on the strategic alternatives we are evaluating for the Michigan Campus and our other portfolio businesses. Our objective is to place these businesses in structures that support their development and make their value more identifiable to our stockholders." The Company reiterates its preliminary consolidated financial guidance for the year ending December 31, 2027, of $300 million to $350 million in revenue and $60 million to $80 million in Adjusted EBITDA. Based upon known and reasonably calculated projections, including management's current operating plans, anticipated customer deployments, expected financing activities, projected digital-asset initiatives and the anticipated performance of the Company's portfolio businesses, this guidance reflects management's current projections. The Company cannot provide a quantitative reconciliation of its projected Adjusted EBITDA to the most directly comparable measure calculated under GAAP, which in this case, would be net income or loss, because certain components required to calculate net income or loss cannot presently be reasonably estimated without unreasonable effort. These components include future interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, impairment charges, acquisition-related expenses and changes in the fair value of financial instruments. These items are likely to be material to the Company's future GAAP results. No definitive decision has been made regarding any strategic alternatives under evaluation. Any discussions or considerations remain preliminary, and no assurances can be given that any definitive terms will be agreed upon or result in any transaction. Any transaction would be subject to further negotiation, due diligence, execution of definitive agreements and applicable corporate and regulatory approvals, including, as applicable, approval by the Company's Board of Directors. There can be no assurance that an agreement will be reached or that, if an agreement is reached, any transaction would ultimately be consummated. No transaction timetable is assured. artigo.texto: Catalisador de célula a combustível ultradurável pode alimentar data centers Um catalisador de célula a combustível recém-desenvolvido e altamente durável pode tornar o hidrogênio uma opção de energia mais viável para data centers de alto consumo energético e outros usos, informa o Hydrogen Central. O relato aborda o trabalho liderado por Gang Wu, professor Elvera e William R. Stuckenberg na McKelvey School of Engineering da Universidade Washington em St. Louis, cujo grupo elaborou um método que pode aprimorar células a combustível de baixa temperatura e ampliar seu papel como fonte alternativa de eletricidade. Os data centers estão se espalhando rapidamente pelos Estados Unidos, adicionando pressão crescente ao fornecimento de energia do país. Esses locais precisam de enormes quantidades de eletricidade tanto para operar seu hardware de computação quanto para resfriá-lo. Segundo o Electric Power Research Institute, os data centers podem representar até 9% da geração anual de eletricidade dos EUA até 2030, ante 4% da demanda total de eletricidade em 2023. Cientistas atualmente investigam formas de aliviar parte dessa pressão. A equipe de pesquisa também contou com especialistas do Brookhaven National Laboratory, do Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, da Northeastern University e da University of Pittsburgh. Seus resultados foram publicados em 6 de agosto de 2026 na Nature Nanotechnology. Wu observou que, quando um data center consegue atender às próprias necessidades de eletricidade por meio de uma célula a combustível, ele converteria hidrogênio e outros combustíveis diretamente em eletricidade, reduzindo a carga sobre a rede elétrica. Tornando as células a combustível mais eficientes e duráveis As células a combustível geram eletricidade ao combinar hidrogênio e oxigênio. Água e calor também são produzidos no processo. Os catalisadores ajudam a acelerar essa reação, ao mesmo tempo em que reduzem as perdas de energia e possibilitam melhor desempenho e vida útil mais longa. Criar um catalisador ideal ainda é um obstáculo significativo. Os catalisadores de célula a combustível atuais continuam aquém de oferecer a combinação de atividade e durabilidade exigida para metas de desempenho essenciais. A platina é considerada uma das substâncias catalisadoras mais eficazes, mas também é um metal precioso. Por isso, os pesquisadores buscam empregar a menor quantidade possível de platina sem enfraquecer o desempenho do catalisador na conversão e no armazenamento de energia. Converter a platina em nanopartículas é um método de fazer um suprimento limitado render mais. Reduzir a platina bruta a partículas extremamente finas aumenta acentuadamente a área de superfície disponível para reações químicas. Isso permite o uso de quantidades mínimas do metal, geralmente menos de um quarto de miligrama por centímetro quadrado. No entanto, as nanopartículas de platina podem se transformar enquanto uma célula a combustível está em operação. Elas podem se dissolver, migrar para outros pontos e aumentar de tamanho, levando o desempenho a se deteriorar com o tempo. Um desafio de longa data dos catalisadores de platina Nos últimos anos, os catalisadores intermetálicos de platina surgiram como uma opção forte em comparação com as ligas de platina padrão, pois podem oferecer melhor atividade e estabilidade. Sua produção, porém, envolve outro tradeoff difícil. Para manter as nanopartículas pequenas, uniformemente dispersas e eficientes no uso da platina, os pesquisadores normalmente recozem os materiais em temperaturas abaixo de 700 graus Celsius. Tais temperaturas são frequentemente baixas demais para impulsionar completamente a mudança de um arranjo atômico desordenado para um altamente ordenado, mudança essa crucial para obter o máximo de atividade e durabilidade dos catalisadores intermetálicos. Wu e seus colaboradores criaram uma nova arquitetura de carbono destinada a superar esse obstáculo. A substância é feita de esferas de carbono porosas e ocas que contêm nanocanais radiais ordenados, além de considerável espaço de poros e área de superfície. Esse design permite que muitas nanopartículas intermetálicas de platina e cobalto permaneçam densamente compactadas e ainda assim uniformemente dispersas. Também possibilita que a estrutura intermetálica ordenada desejada se forme em temperaturas muito mais altas sem fazer as nanopartículas se agregarem. Por meio dessa abordagem, os pesquisadores conseguiram enfrentar um tradeoff difícil entre obter uma estrutura atômica altamente ordenada e preservar uma distribuição uniforme de partículas de catalisador extremamente pequenas. Wu explicou que a estratégia emprega a nova nanoestrutura de carbono para sintetizar nanopartículas intermetálicas de platina e cobalto capazes de reduzir o teor de metal precioso ao mesmo tempo em que aumentam a atividade e a estabilidade. Ele observou que, historicamente, haveria um tradeoff entre tamanho e estabilidade, mas com o hospedeiro de nanocanais de carbono ordenados, as nanopartículas de platina e cobalto podem ser confinadas e permanecer estáveis em tamanho de partícula muito pequeno mesmo em altas temperaturas. Pequenos canais de carbono ajudam a platina a durar mais Partículas de catalisador maiores podem aumentar a estabilidade, mas isso frequentemente custa atividade. Outros métodos que favorecem a atividade podem abrir mão da estabilidade de longo prazo. A equipe de Wu buscou garantir ambos ao construir um suporte de carbono nanoestruturado com pequenos canais dispostos em arranjo radial. Os pesquisadores também regularam meticulosamente o tamanho e o volume dos poros. Durante os testes, o material manteve 85% de seu desempenho após 150.000 ciclos severos de tensão. Os pesquisadores calculam que isso pode equivaler a cerca de 25.000 horas de operação. artigo.texto: Ainda existem muitos obstáculos que impedem que terrenos pós-mineração gerem créditos de carbono. Áreas de terra não afetadas pela extração mineral têm potencial para reflorestamento, mas para gerar créditos de carbono, requisitos adicionais relativos à reposição, custo e acesso ao mercado devem ser atendidos. O Sr. Nguyen Trung Thong, especialista em financiamento de carbono da CARE Vietnam, conversou com um repórter do jornal Indústria e Comércio sobre soluções baseadas na natureza para a restauração florestal após a exploração mineral e sobre as oportunidades de participação no mercado de carbono. A restauração florestal abre oportunidades para créditos de carbono. Senhor, de que forma a restauração florestal após a exploração mineral pode abrir oportunidades de participação no mercado de carbono? Sr. Nguyen Trung Thong: A exploração mineral está frequentemente associada à exigência de que as empresas desenvolvam um plano de encerramento da mina. Este plano inclui atividades para garantir a segurança ambiental, a restauração ecológica e a recuperação da paisagem. Ele pode servir de base para a implementação de atividades de reflorestamento e restauração florestal. No entanto, o reflorestamento para restauração ambiental e a geração de créditos de carbono são duas coisas diferentes. De acordo com as regulamentações atuais, as empresas devem manter a floresta por três anos, e os créditos de carbono só podem ser calculados a partir do quarto ano. Portanto, a questão crucial é demonstrar a complementaridade de carbono do projeto. Em outras palavras, a questão que precisa ser respondida é: se não houver um projeto de carbono, como essa floresta será mantida a partir do quarto ano? Se a empresa ainda for obrigada a realizar atividades de restauração completas, conforme as obrigações legais, a redução das emissões ou a absorção de carbono decorrente dessas atividades pode não atender aos requisitos de complementaridade. Este é um ponto que exige estudo e avaliação cuidadosos ao se considerar a possibilidade de implantação de projetos de carbono em áreas após a exploração mineral. Então, quais são as oportunidades para as áreas após a exploração, senhor? Sr. Nguyen Trung Thong: Um ponto importante a destacar é que, em muitas áreas após a exploração, a orientação de uso da terra a longo prazo ainda não está clara. Enquanto isso, a restauração florestal é uma direção relativamente clara em termos de meio ambiente e paisagem. Do ponto de vista do mercado de carbono, essas áreas poderiam abrir espaço para projetos de reflorestamento. No entanto, para se tornar um projeto de carbono, além dos requisitos de reflorestamento, existem muitas condições específicas relativas à metodologia, à linha de base, à complementaridade, ao tempo de implementação e à capacidade de medir a absorção de carbono. Portanto, não se deve presumir que o simples reflorestamento após a exploração madeireira gerará créditos de carbono. É necessária uma avaliação separada para determinar se o projeto realmente gera redução ou absorção adicional de emissões. Os custos e as condições de mercado determinam as oportunidades de investimento. Alguns argumentam que a área total das minas pode chegar a milhares de hectares, mas a área investida em restauração é limitada, e o custo da restauração também representa um problema para as empresas. Qual a sua opinião sobre essa questão? Você também pode gostar Sr. Nguyen Trung Thong: Precisamos separar duas questões. Se a restauração é uma obrigação legal, então a mineradora deve cumpri-la. Ela deve plantar árvores de acordo com a densidade e as espécies especificadas e cuidar delas dentro do prazo estipulado. Essa é uma obrigação que a empresa deve cumprir, independentemente de gerar ou não receita com carbono. No entanto, a questão é se, após esse período, a área restaurada realmente se transformará em uma floresta e como ela será mantida. Essa ainda é uma questão que precisa de mais esclarecimentos. Se os investidores desejarem estender o processo de recuperação a partir do quarto ano para formar um projeto de carbono, deverão incluir todos esses custos na equação financeira. Somente quando os custos incorridos puderem gerar benefícios com créditos de carbono é que os investidores terão uma base para considerar o projeto. Portanto, a viabilidade dos projetos depende não apenas da área do terreno, mas também do custo, do tempo e do valor do carbono que pode ser gerado. - Do ponto de vista de um investidor, quais são as condições necessárias para que projetos de restauração florestal após a exploração mineral atraiam capital? Sr. Nguyen Trung Thong: Na minha opinião, a partir do quarto ano, os investidores estarão preocupados , em primeiro lugar, com as obrigações legais. Se as obrigações legais continuarem a exigir que a empresa mantenha a área florestal, então o projeto de carbono precisa demonstrar como contribui para isso. Esta é uma questão muito importante. Em segundo lugar , há a questão da dimensão do terreno. As áreas pós-mineração podem gerar áreas significativas para projetos de restauração, embora nem todos os setores disponham de terrenos adequados. Em terceiro lugar , há o momento de início do projeto. Para projetos de reflorestamento, as normas têm requisitos específicos quanto às condições da área antes da implementação. De acordo com as normas vietnamitas, um projeto deve considerar o estado da área como não florestada durante três anos antes do início; algumas normas internacionais podem exigir um período mais longo. Se as áreas pós-mineração atenderem a esses requisitos, podem representar uma área de interesse significativa. No entanto, uma avaliação específica de cada área e projeto ainda é necessária. Assim, em comparação com outros setores, quais são os aspectos notáveis da extração mineral sob a perspectiva do investimento em carbono? artigo.texto: Key Stats for Amazon Stock - Price change for Amazon stock in last 6 months: 18% - $AMZN Stock Price as of Oct. 2: $252 - 52-Week High: $287 - $AMZN Stock Price Target: $331 What Happened? Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) said its cloud unit will invest more than $1 billion over the next five years. The money will go to US communities that host its data centers. Amazon Web Services made the announcement on Friday. The plan covers education, job training, and energy affordability. It also covers water and energy preservation. AWS also promised to tackle the impact of its data centers on electricity and water use. The move makes sense. Data centers power and run AI models. But communities across the US have pushed back. They worry about electricity demand and utility costs. AWS noted that more than 100 data center moratoriums are being considered nationwide. The backlash is also a political issue ahead of the US midterm elections on November 3. Amazon said it invested $276 billion in data centers between 2011 and 2025. It has large projects or expansions planned in Indiana, Louisiana, North Carolina, Virginia, and Mississippi. AWS CEO Matt Garman said the buildout is urgent. He said other countries also see the benefits of AI. He added that the countries leading in AI will shape it. AWS also said it will be water positive by 2030. That means it will return more water to communities than it uses. It says it is 75% of the way there. What the Market Is Telling Us About Amazon Stock $1 billion is small compared with what Amazon spends. On the Q2 call, management said it expects about $220 billion in cash capex this year. Most of that supports AI and AWS. So this pledge is more about public trust than cost. That trust matters for Amazon stock. AWS is the growth engine. Revenue rose 36.7% last quarter, its fastest pace in 18 quarters. Backlog reached $496 billion. AWS also posted $16.6 billion in operating income. Management says demand is higher than capacity. It expects that to stay true in 2027. New data centers are how Amazon meets that demand. If local opposition slows approvals, that could hold back growth. That is the real risk for Amazon stock. Amazon also said it plans to double its power capacity by the end of 2027 from 2025 levels. Community support will help make that possible. For now, the market will likely stay focused on AWS growth and capex returns. Still, rising local pushback is worth watching. Any new moratoriums could affect how investors view Amazon stock. A clear community plan may ease some of that worry for Amazon stockholders.

artigo.texto: Amazon warns $68 billion in blocked data centers threatens US AI lead — AWS CEO decries 100 proposed bans, pledges $1B community fund Various countries intentionally seeding misinformation in the U.S. about data centers to trick us into slowing down - AWS CEO Amazon has issued grave warnings to communities opposing data centers, stating that their actions could cause irreversible damage to the U.S. economy and national security. In a lengthy 3000-word post earlier today, October 2, CEO of Amazon Web Services (AWS), Matt Garman detailed the many benefits of Artificial Intelligence, comparing the technology’s impact on the economy to those of modern transportation systems and the Internet, before attempting to debunk “myths” around data centers and calling on local communities to be more receptive to build-outs as a matter of national urgency. The post also details Amazon's plans to do more for data center host communities through its “Built Together” community investment frameworks. After outlining AI’s impact and the need for data center buildouts, Garman explained why it was imperative for the U.S. to lead the AI race. “The countries that lead in AI will shape it and get the most from it in the short and long run. The choices we make today will determine that outcome, and a lapse in our nation’s focus or resolve could put us behind, and potentially irreparably so,” he wrote, presenting urgent buildouts as a key factor in leading that race. Next, Garman addressed growing anti-data center movements that have reportedly blocked data center projects worth $68 billion in the second quarter of 2026 alone, warning that if the 100 data center moratoriums being considered across the country should go through, “the US could be writing its own losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations.” He also pointed out that unlike transportation infrastructure, the comparably critical data center buildout is not funded by taxpayer money, but by private firms. The post dismissed many of the concerns about the buildouts as myths, then proceeded to attempt to debunk them. Garman said that, contrary to popular belief, “Data centers actually use very little water relative to other industries,” a position many hyperscalers have repeated. Amazon earlier claimed that its data centers consume only 0.075% of the water Americans use to water their lawns and gardens. Garman also claims the narrative that data centers are driving up energy bills is “misleading and convenient scapegoating.” He argues that AI is simply precipitating an expansion of power infrastructure that was always bound to happen. “Once we collectively build out this new capacity, again funded by the private sector, it should lead to flat or lower rates in the future for residents living in communities with these expanded grids,” he said. On the other hand, contradictory reports claim that AI data centers trigger a "massive irreversible" 76% electricity price spike. The U.S. House also recently passed a bill that directed regulators to consider making AI data centers pay for grid upgrades to minimize the impact on residents. The bill was eventually rejected in the Senate, with opponents saying it was "toothless" and didn't do enough to protect residents. Speaking on pollution, Garman says that data centers emitting huge amounts of pollution with their large backup diesel generators is a myth. He claims that while data centers have rarely used backup power in case of a power outage, this is only necessary because many industries depend on the facilities. This claim doesn’t exactly address growing concerns of pollution from gas turbines powering off-grid data centers. Elon Musk recently came under fire for using unlicensed gas turbines at the Colossus data center. Lastly, Garman said claims that communities do not benefit from data centers are false, citing “considerable tax revenue, positive economic impact, large numbers of good jobs, and education programs” as some of the benefits to the communities where data centers are built. Microsoft pledged to invest $1 billion in local infrastructure improvements in its Hyperion data center community and had reportedly awarded $1.6 billion in contracts to local businesses since construction began, in addition to paying teacher bonuses. As benefits specifically on Amazon’s part, Garman listed an estimated $3 billion in taxes to St. Joseph County, Indiana, over time; more than $1 billion already contributed to communities across the U.S.; thousands of jobs created in building and running the data centers; and education programs with over 10,000 educators and learners enrolled. Through its “Built Together” initiative, Amazon says it will “add more than $1 billion over the next five years to what we’re already doing — with communities in the driver’s seat to determine what’s most useful for them across education, job training, energy affordability, water and energy preservation, and local priorities.” Garman insists that data centers can’t be separated from the revolutionary impact of AI. U.S. President Donald Trump appears to agree, at least on the “revolutionary impact” aspect, and has repeatedly expressed a desire to maintain a lead over China. On the other hand, data center critics claim that responsible implementation of the build-outs, and not AI itself, is the bone of contention. artigo.texto: Stocktwits Zero To Sixty — Tesla Deliveries Clear The Street, BYD Widens The Gap, Rivian Holds Forecast, Ford And GM EV Sales Fall Hard - Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, about 25,000 above the company-compiled consensus of 461,974. - Tesla’s biggest rival, Chinese EV giant BYD, meanwhile, sold 1,323,065 new-energy vehicles in the same quarter, including 762,478 BEVs. - GM and Ford reported deep drops in EV deliveries in the period. Electric vehicle demand was the key focus this week, with several names, including EV giant Tesla, announcing its Q3 delivery numbers. Tesla beat delivery estimates. The beat still left it down 2.1% from a year earlier, and further behind BYD, which sold 762,478 battery-electric passenger cars in the quarter, a lead of about 276,000. Rivian also topped estimates with a record 19,248 and kept its full-year guide. The legacy names, however, did not get the same lift. General Motors and Ford reported steep drops in U.S. electric sales against a year-ago quarter inflated by the expiring federal tax credit. Tesla Clears The Street, BYD Widens The Gap Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, about 25,000 above the company-compiled consensus of 461,974. It built 464,391, so deliveries outpaced production by 22,141 as the company kept working down inventory. Total deliveries were up 1.3% from the second quarter and down 2.1% from 497,099 a year earlier, a period inflated by buyers rushing to claim the U.S. federal tax credit before it expired. Model 3 and Model Y accounted for 478,237 of the deliveries. The rest, including the stainless steel Cybertruck, accounted for 8,295, down 48% from a year ago. Through three quarters, Tesla has delivered 1,324,681 vehicles, up 8.8% from the same point in 2025. Tesla’s biggest rival, Chinese EV giant BYD, meanwhile, sold 1,323,065 new-energy vehicles in the same quarter, up 18.8% from a year earlier and 19.4% from the second quarter. The number includes plug-in hybrids and a small number of commercial vehicles, not just battery-electric passenger cars. For battery-electric passenger cars, the gap remains wide. BYD sold 762,478 of them in the quarter, up 30.9% from a year earlier and 36.9% from the second quarter. That is 275,946 more than Tesla delivered, a lead of about 57%. In the second quarter, the gap was just about 77,000. Beyond the sales print, Tesla said it plans to start making its own 4680 battery cells in Grünheide in 2027 and build that plant to 18 gigawatt-hours a year. The stated aim is to make the cell and the finished car on one European site. Rivian Sets A Record: The Full-Year Guide Stays Put Rivian delivered a record 19,248 vehicles, up about 46% from a year earlier and ahead of expectations near 18,000. Production was 19,751. It was the first full quarter with the smaller R2 on the road, so far only in the higher-priced Performance version, priced just under $60,000. The company reaffirmed 2026 delivery guidance of 65,000 to 70,000, which means the fourth quarter still has to clear roughly 23,000 vehicles to hit the bottom of the range. Ford And GM Give Back The Credit Rush Ford sold 6,047 electric vehicles in the U.S. in the quarter, down 80.2% from a record 30,612 a year earlier. Electric models were 1.2% of Ford’s 509,764 U.S. sales, down from 5.6%. Total Ford sales fell 6.6%. General Motors sold 25,473 electric vehicles, down 61.7% from 66,501. Electric models were 3.8% of GM’s 670,974 U.S. sales, down from 9.4%. Overall GM sales fell 5.5%. Excluding electric models, they were about flat. artigo.texto: India’s emerging carbon economy is beginning to connect sectors that have traditionally been treated separately: sugar, ethanol, renewable gas, agriculture, waste management, carbon removal and climate finance. Sugar mills are no longer only food-processing enterprises. They are increasingly becoming integrated biorefineries with access to bagasse, molasses, press mud, spent wash, sugarcane trash, biogas and other biomass streams. These resources can support electricity generation, ethanol, compressed biogas, biochar, soil amendments and potentially carbon-removal projects. The central question is no longer whether these activities can produce environmental benefits. The more important question is whether those benefits can be measured, verified, monetised and converted into dependable project revenues. Sugarcane as a carbon sink Dr. Sanjay Kolte, IAS, Commissioner of Sugar, Government of Maharashtra, highlighted the opportunity for sugar mills to participate in the offset side of India’s emerging carbon market. That opportunity follows from the biological and industrial characteristics of sugarcane. Sugarcane is a C4 crop with a highly efficient photosynthetic pathway suited to warm, high-light environments. It can produce substantial biomass and absorb significant quantities of atmospheric carbon dioxide during growth. Carbon is temporarily stored in the stalks, leaves and roots, while some carbon can enter the soil through roots, residues and organic matter. Research has identified sugarcane and agricultural soils as having meaningful carbon-sequestration potential. However, sugarcane should not be described as a permanently storing carbon sink merely because it absorbs carbon dioxide during growth. Much of the carbon fixed in the plant is released when the cane is harvested, processed, combusted or decomposed. The relevant climate benefit depends on the complete carbon balance, including fertiliser use, irrigation, diesel consumption, transport, processing, residue management and the end use of sugar, ethanol, electricity or other products. A sugarcane-based carbon project must therefore calculate net mitigation rather than gross photosynthetic uptake. It must establish a credible baseline and account for emissions throughout the relevant project boundary. It must also distinguish temporary biological carbon storage from durable removal. A sugar mill can strengthen its carbon position by reducing fossil-fuel consumption through bagasse-based energy, avoiding open burning or unmanaged decomposition of residues, converting organic waste into biogas or compressed biogas, improving soil organic carbon, producing and applying biochar, reducing methane emissions from effluent or manure, displacing fossil fuels with ethanol or renewable electricity, and measuring emissions across the farm-to-factory value chain. This creates an opportunity for sugar mills to participate in the offset mechanism of the Indian Carbon Market. But the opportunity will depend on approved methodologies, monitoring, reporting and verification, as well as proof that the credited activity is additional and not simply the result of an existing legal obligation or commercially attractive investment. The sugar mill as a biorefinery The modern sugar mill can be understood as a biorefinery rather than a single-product factory. Bagasse can generate renewable electricity and process heat. Molasses can be converted into ethanol. Press mud and spent wash can be treated and used in soil applications or anaerobic digestion. Sugarcane trash can become feedstock for biomass energy, compressed biogas or biochar, provided its removal does not damage soil health. This integrated model creates several possible economic streams: sugar, ethanol, renewable electricity, compressed biogas, renewable-gas attributes, renewable-energy certificates, carbon credits, biochar and avoided waste-treatment costs. The central challenge is the separation of environmental attributes. If the same tonne of biogas is used to issue a renewable-gas certificate and also claimed as a carbon credit, the accounting system must determine whether both claims are permissible and how they should be adjusted. Similarly, renewable electricity may generate a Renewable Energy Certificate, but its associated emissions reduction cannot automatically be counted again as a separate carbon credit. Environmental attributes must therefore be defined, tracked, transferred and retired through a transparent registry. This is the difference between a credible environmental market and a collection of overlapping claims. Ethanol and the policy signal India’s ethanol programme has created one of the country’s strongest policy signals for bio-based energy. Under the Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme, blending increased from less than 1.5 per cent in 2013–14 to 20 per cent in the 2025–26 ethanol supply year. The National Policy on Biofuels, as amended in 2022, advanced the 20 per cent blending target from 2030 to the 2025–26 supply year. The increase in blending has been driven by several objectives, including reducing crude-oil imports, improving energy security, creating demand for agricultural feedstocks and supporting the sugar industry during periods of surplus production. It has also strengthened the commercial case for distilleries and sugar mills investing in ethanol capacity. Maharashtra is central to this transition because of its substantial sugarcane and sugar-processing base. Dr. Kolte referred to 156 ethanol units in Maharashtra. The precise interpretation of this number depends on whether it refers to operational units, approved distilleries, attached distilleries or the broader registered project universe. It should therefore be used with a clear definition in any formal publication. artigo.texto: Amazon investirá US$ 1 bilhão em comunidades de data centers nos EUA A divisão de computação em nuvem da Amazon afirmou nesta sexta-feira (2) que investirá mais de US$ 1 bilhão nos próximos cinco anos em comunidades dos Estados Unidos onde possui data centers e prometeu combater os impactos dessas instalações no consumo de eletricidade e água. Os centros de dados, que fornecem o poder computacional para treinar e executar modelos de IA, têm enfrentado oposição em comunidades de todo o país devido a preocupações com a demanda de eletricidade, custos de serviços públicos e outros impactos locais. Essa reação negativa representa um desafio político para os republicanos às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA, em 3 de novembro. A Amazon afirmou ter investido US$ 276 bilhões em data centers entre 2011 e 2025, e que tinha grandes projetos ou expansões em andamento em muitos estados, incluindo Indiana, Louisiana, Carolina do Norte, Virgínia e Mississippi. A Amazon Web Services (AWS) afirmou que os planos de investimento comunitário anunciados na sexta-feira incluirão gastos com educação, treinamento profissional, acessibilidade energética, preservação de água e energia e outras prioridades locais em partes dos EUA onde possui infraestrutura. Em um longo comunicado, a empresa procurou refutar as críticas relacionadas aos impactos ambientais, energéticos e econômicos dos data centers, e observou que mais de 100 moratórias estavam sendo consideradas em todo o país. “Há urgência na construção deste data center porque não somos o único país que vê os benefícios da IA para a economia e a segurança nacional, e os países que lideram em IA irão moldá-la e tirar o máximo proveito dela”, disse Matt Garman, CEO da AWS. A AWS também se comprometeu a ser positiva em relação à água em todos os seus data centers até 2030, devolvendo mais água às comunidades do que utiliza, e afirmou estar 75% perto de atingir essa meta. Fonte:CNN Brasil

artigo.texto: LG Electronics expands chiller production for AI data centers The company plans to invest a total of USD 110 million in a new air-cooled chiller production facility in the US and in expanding two air-cooled chiller production lines in South Korea. LG Electronics (LG) is expanding its chiller manufacturing capabilities with a new production facility in the United States and increased production capacity in South Korea, further strengthening its ability to deliver end-to-end cooling solutions for AI data centers (AIDCs). The company’s new air-cooled chiller production facility in Windsor, Virginia will produce air-cooled chillers for AIDCs, with production scheduled to begin in the first half of 2027. The facility’s chiller production will support a stable, responsive supply system for rising demand across North America, while serving as a strategic base for LG’s regional expansion, the company said. LG is also expanding its air-cooled chiller production lines in Pyeongtaek and Changwon, South Korea. The company is improving operational efficiency by adopting a conveyor-based production system designed for mass production. The company plans to invest a total of KRW 150 billion (about USD 110 million) in its new US facility and its factories in Pyeongtaek and Changwon. LG is also broadening its AIDC thermal management business through its Chip-to-Chiller solution strategy. The portfolio includes chillers, Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs) and cold plates that absorb heat directly from chips. LG is pursuing additional AIDC projects in North America through its relationships with leading hyperscalers and big tech companies. In Asia, LG is applying its “One LG” strategy by combining heating, ventilation and air conditioning technologies with battery solutions and data center design, build and operation capabilities from other LG affiliates. LG is also applying this integrated approach to Sinar Mas Group’s hyperscale AIDC project in Jakarta, Indonesia, the company said. “We will continue to strengthen our core capabilities in AI data center cooling solutions, from differentiated product technologies to production capacity,” said James Lee, president of the LG Eco Solution Company. “With these capabilities, we will ensure a stable supply and actively address rapidly growing market demand.”

artigo.texto: Desperdício de comida agora pode gerar créditos de carbono Nova modalidade de crédito de carbono busca unir redução de emissões, combate ao desperdício de alimentos e segurança alimentar Se uma empresa quiser reduzir sua pegada de carbono, pode comprar créditos de carbono emitidos pela Verra, o maior programa de certificação de créditos de carbono do mundo. Esses créditos podem ser destinados a projetos como energia renovável ou restauração de florestas, permitindo que uma empresa reivindique os benefícios ambientais de um novo parque eólico ou de árvores plantadas em uma área que havia sido desmatada. Agora existe uma nova opção: créditos de carbono para alimentos resgatados, que ajudam a financiar organizações que coletam alimentos que seriam desperdiçados e os distribuem para pessoas necessitadas. Esses créditos emitidos pela Verra agora estão disponíveis graças à Brightly, uma startup de Boston fundada em 2023 por Andy Levitt, que anteriormente fundou e comandou a Purple Carrot, uma empresa de kits de refeições à base de plantas. A Brightly já tem contratos com mais de 25 organizações de resgate de alimentos. Agora, porém, seus créditos de carbono relacionados ao desperdício de alimentos estão sendo emitidos pela Verra, tornando-os os primeiros do tipo dentro da metodologia do padrão de certificação para reduzir a perda e o desperdício de alimentos. Os créditos de carbono são cercados de controvérsias. Pesquisas descobriram que alguns projetos não entregaram benefícios climáticos reais; especialistas afirmam que a possibilidade de usar créditos pode permitir o greenwashing. Levitt sabe que existe desconfiança em relação ao mercado de carbono, mas afirma que a solução da Brightly cria um “ciclo virtuoso de atividade” que financia ainda mais o resgate de alimentos, permitindo que organizações sem fins lucrativos alimentem mais pessoas. “Agora somos capazes de oferecer uma solução inovadora para empresas que querem se concentrar em enfrentar tanto os desafios ambientais quanto a fome”, diz Levitt. “É uma categoria e uma classe completamente novas de créditos de carbono que existem no mercado.” Reduzir o desperdício de alimentos é uma maneira clara de enfrentar as mudanças climáticas. Globalmente, o desperdício de alimentos responde por entre 6% e 10% das emissões mundiais. A aviação, para comparação, responde por cerca de 3%. Ao mesmo tempo, dezenas de milhões de americanos têm acesso limitado ou incerto a alimentos e dependem de bancos de alimentos ou despensas comunitárias para complementar suas compras. A Feeding America estima que cerca de 50 milhões de americanos receberam assistência alimentar de organizações beneficentes em 2023. Muitas dessas organizações, porém, enfrentam dificuldades de financiamento, especialmente diante do aumento da demanda provocado pela alta dos preços dos alimentos e pelo estresse econômico generalizado. ENFRENTANDO O DESAFIO AMBIENTAL E A FOME A Brightly afirma que sua solução enfrenta os dois lados dessa questão. “Nosso objetivo é criar financiamento sustentável para organizações sem fins lucrativos de resgate de alimentos, permitindo que elas mantenham os alimentos fora dos aterros sanitários e alimentem pessoas que passam fome”, diz Levitt. Ao financiar o resgate de alimentos, a Brightly afirma evitar que o metano emitido pelo desperdício de alimentos chegue à atmosfera. Uma parte fundamental de um crédito de carbono eficaz é a adicionalidade, o que significa que a redução das emissões não teria acontecido de qualquer maneira sem a receita gerada pelo crédito de carbono. A Brightly afirma quantificar os benefícios de seus créditos de carbono coletando um histórico de três anos da atividade de uma organização de resgate de alimentos, estabelecendo uma linha de base para o benefício ambiental gerado por aquela organização. A empresa contabiliza apenas o impacto ambiental que excede essa linha de base. Essas organizações sem fins lucrativos coletam todos os tipos de alimentos; algumas podem se concentrar em frutas, legumes e verduras, enquanto outras trabalham com produtos não perecíveis. Cada um desses alimentos tem seu próprio impacto ambiental. A Brightly analisa todos os dados fornecidos pelas organizações sobre o que foi resgatado e em que quantidade, atribuindo um impacto climático a cada tipo de alimento, do pão à carne. “Isso é tratado em um nível hiper específico, linha por linha, alimento por alimento, para alcançar esse grau de precisão e conservadorismo necessário para obter uma classificação de crédito de carbono de alta qualidade”, diz Levitt. Empresas que vão de fabricantes de alimentos a supermercados, e até mesmo companhias de fora do setor alimentício, como empresas de vestuário, poderiam comprar os créditos da Brightly relacionados ao desperdício de alimentos. A Brightly repassa até 80% da receita obtida com a venda dos créditos para as organizações de resgate de alimentos, financiando seus esforços e permitindo que elas ampliem suas operações. É difícil especificar quanto, em dólares, uma organização média de resgate de alimentos poderia receber, diz Levitt, porque os créditos de carbono não são criados individualmente para cada organização; em vez disso, as ações daquela organização representam uma parte de um conjunto maior de créditos. A empresa também já contratou vendas futuras de mais de 80 mil créditos. Com a notícia de que a Verra está emitindo os créditos da Brightly, Levitt espera que esse impacto cresça. A Brightly espera emitir 300 mil créditos por ano, com base em projetos de resgate de alimentos nos Estados Unidos. A empresa também está trabalhando em projetos no exterior. artigo.texto: Dive Brief: - The U.S. Department of Commerce has approved a request from American Battery Technology Co. to export and sell up to $100 million of its recycled black mass from batteries. The decision comes a few months after federal export controls went into place, banning most exports of the material. - American Battery said it sought an exemption from the ban because the United States’ battery collection and shredding infrastructure has developed faster than its domestic downstream refining capacity. - The Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security recently announced temporary export ban until Aug. 27, 2027. It specifies that black mass producers must allocate 100% of monthly sales to domestic buyers unless granted an exception. The rule also applies to exports of tungsten. Dive Insight: ABTC has been working to build up its battery recycling and manufacturing infrastructure as the U.S. continues to focus on shoring up domestic supplies of critical minerals to compete more directly in the global market. The U.S. government sees critical materials as a national security priority, as China currently corners the market on such materials. The black-mass ban rule states that “the inadequate supply of [critical minerals and materials] poses an increasing risk to our national defense and security,” and an export ban would ”take immediate action to secure the supply of recoverable CMMs.” Much of ABTC’s recycling process focuses on black mass, which includes shredded lithium-ion battery scrap that contains cathode material typically made up of lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese as well as other materials. The company said in a statement that access to “carefully managed export channels” would allow ABTC to continue operations and build up its recycling infrastructure “while that refining gap closes.” ABTC is among the companies that have sought an exception to the export ban. The rule specifies that companies can apply for an exception if they sends materials outside the country for processing or refining with the intent that the refined materials would be returned to the United States. Other exceptions could be granted for companies that would experience “undue hardship” if exports were blocked, or for scenarios where a blocked export would somehow lead to a reduced domestic supply of critical minerals, among other reasons. The company is “grateful for this license and continued support from the U.S. government for the sales of our domestic critical mineral products,” CEO Ryan Melsert said in a statement. Its operations, which also include work to build a separate commercial-scale lithium hydroxide refinery, are supported by grants from the U.S. Department of Energy. Its lithium refinery in Nevada is funded partly from a $57 million DOE grant. ABTC continues to ramp up operations at its critical mineral recycling facility in Nevada, which is designed to take shipments of large-scale batteries from OEMs and process the material into black mass and other recovered materials like copper, aluminum and steel. The company’s feedstock comes partly from battery energy storage systems that once supported data centers and AI facilities, as well as end of life electric vehicle batteries and consumer electronics. The Department of Commerce’s decision to give ABTC a black mass export license shows that the company has proved its reliability, and strengthens the company’s market position, Melsert said in a statement.

artigo.texto: East Hampton, Montauk battery plants to temporarily close under Suffolk pact The owners of two contested battery energy storage plants on the East End agreed to temporarily suspend operations starting Friday night following behind-the-scenes negotiations with Suffolk County. The plants, on Cove Hollow Road in East Hampton and another in Montauk, were scheduled to be shut down by 7 p.m. Friday, said Suffolk County Executive Edward P. Romaine in an interview. The agreement with the county doesn’t include specifics on a remediation plan, which will be conducted by the state, county officials said. The plants won’t restart operations until the remediation work is complete, they said. Romaine said he expected the fire suppression systems in the plants to be removed over the next few weeks. The system at the Cove Hollow Road plant is suspected to be the cause of groundwater contamination directly around the facility and at now-shuttered drinking water wells up to 2,500 feet away. He also demanded that the state release a remediation plan for the East Hampton site. The state Department of Environmental Conservation has said it will be released in early fall, following a probe of the toxic plume. artigo.texto: The Bugatti Veyron is already one of the most recognizable hypercars of its era, but the Black Bess Edition takes its exclusivity even further. Amian Exclusive Cars in Germany offered one of the rare Veyron 16.4 Black Bess cars, which the dealer identifies as one of just three built as part of Bugatti’s Legends series. The particular car featured in the listing was first registered in 2014 and has just 2,600 miles on the odometer. It is finished in black and has had a single previous owner. Bugatti quotes 1,184 horsepower and 1,500 Nm of torque between 3,000 and 5,000 rpm for the Legends editions, from a quad-turbocharged W16 engine. Power is sent to all four wheels through a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Performance is a major part of the Veyron’s appeal. The dealer lists a top speed of 253 mph and a 0–100 mph time of 5.9 seconds. The specification also includes active aerodynamics, and the dealer highlights the car’s bespoke interior and exterior treatment. The Black Bess is the fifth of Bugatti’s six Legends editions and is based on the Veyron 16.4 Grand Sport Vitesse, finished in black with gold accents. The dealer says the car will be checked at a nearby Bugatti dealer before handover. The price is listed as “On request,” and the listing is now marked as sold. Speaking of the Veyron 16.4 Grand Sport Vitesse, we’re reminded of F1 driver Fernando Alonso’s recent purchase. The Aston Martin driver bought a similar luxury hypercar, but his 16.4 Grand Sport Vitesse comes with a polished aluminum body that gives it an appearance unlike most other examples, MotorBiscuit reported. A video shows Alonso cruising through Monaco in the striking Veyron, with its chrome-look reflecting the sunlight like a mirror. He briefly stops at an intersection before pulling away again, giving the distinctive Bugatti plenty of time to catch the attention of onlookers and passing traffic. This Veyron’s extraordinary appearance comes from its construction, not a conventional chrome finish. Its body panels were reportedly carved from solid aluminum blocks and subsequently polished to create the highly reflective surface. The process was extremely material-intensive, reportedly requiring more than 20 tons of aluminum before the one-off bodywork was completed. The extensive bodywork modifications came with an enormous price tag, though. The extra expense of creating the bespoke body was roughly equal to the price of another new Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse. Notably, it is not known how much Alonso paid to make this Veyron a part of his personal collection.

artigo.texto: Solid-state batteries have long been heralded as the next great leap in energy storage, promising to replace the flammable liquid electrolytes inside today’s lithium-ion cells with solid materials that could make devices safer and more energy dense. Yet a persistent engineering problem has slowed their progress: the solid materials that shuttle lithium ions between electrodes are often stiff and unforgiving, struggling to maintain the intimate contact with electrode surfaces that a working battery demands. Now, researchers at Rice University have taken an unusually elegant approach to that problem by asking a question that most electrolyte designers have overlooked — what if the material that carries the ions could also bend, flex, and adapt mechanically to the environment inside a cell? The Rice team, drawn from the departments of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, Chemistry, and Materials Science and Nanoengineering, along with the Rice Advanced Materials Institute, has developed a relatively soft and flexible porous material that selectively transports lithium ions. The work, published in the peer-reviewed journal Chemical Science, introduces a new design philosophy for porous solid electrolytes, one that treats mechanical adaptability not as an afterthought but as a core performance criterion, sitting alongside ionic conductivity and chemical stability in the designer’s toolkit. The material at the heart of the study is called ZnBTCA, and it belongs to a family of compounds known as metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs. These are porous crystalline materials built from metal atoms connected by organic molecules into repeating, lattice-like structures. What makes MOFs so compelling for battery applications is their architecture: they contain tiny, ordered channels whose size and chemistry can be tailored to move or hold specific molecules and ions. In principle, a MOF can act as a molecular sieve for charge, allowing lithium ions to stream through its pores while blocking everything else. Many MOFs previously explored as battery electrolytes, however, have been constructed from relatively rigid aromatic linkers — the organic struts that connect the metal nodes — which produce frameworks that are stiff and mechanically unyielding. ZnBTCA takes a fundamentally different route. Instead of an aromatic linker, it employs a flexible aliphatic linker, an organic molecule with a pliable carbon-chain backbone. That single design choice ripples through the entire material: the framework itself becomes softer and more mechanically adaptable, capable of deforming and conforming rather than resisting. The researchers also emphasized practicality in their selection of building blocks. The material is assembled from relatively abundant, low-cost components, including zinc — one of the most accessible metals in the battery chemist’s repertoire — and an inexpensive aliphatic linker, an important consideration if such materials are ever to move from the laboratory bench toward real-world manufacturing. First author Zina Deriche, a graduate student in chemical and biomolecular engineering at Rice, framed the shift in thinking that underpins the work. MOF electrolytes, she noted, are often designed primarily around how effectively they transport ions. The Rice study demonstrates that the mechanical properties of the framework can also be an important part of the design equation. It is a deceptively simple reframing, but one with significant consequences: a material that can flex with the battery as it charges and discharges may hold up better over thousands of cycles than one that cracks or delaminates under mechanical stress. The dual functionality of ZnBTCA is what excites the team most. The material’s flexible molecular building blocks make it relatively soft, while its negatively charged framework structure favors the movement of positively charged lithium ions through its channels. Stavroula Alina Kampouri, a corresponding author of the study and assistant professor across chemical and biomolecular engineering, chemistry, and materials science and nanoengineering, described the convergence of these properties as the most thrilling aspect of the result. The same material, she explained, brings together flexible building blocks that make the framework softer and more adaptable with a negatively charged structure that promotes selective lithium-ion transport. Bringing those properties together, she said, offers a new way to design MOF electrolytes by considering how ions move and how the material behaves mechanically at the same time. The experimental results lend strong support to the design concept. The researchers first exchanged the sodium ions residing within the framework for lithium ions, a process known as ion exchange that is common in MOF chemistry. After the exchange, they found that roughly 95 percent of the mobile charge-balancing ions in the material were lithium, while the framework itself remained structurally intact — a critical demonstration that the delicate crystalline lattice could survive the swapping of its guest ions without collapsing. Selectivity matters enormously in an electrolyte: a material that carries only lithium ions, rather than a mixed crowd of mobile species, delivers cleaner, more efficient battery operation and helps prevent parasitic reactions that degrade performance over time. Further electrochemical testing quantified just how selective the material is. In measurements of the current flowing through the material, lithium ions accounted for approximately 79 percent of the total ionic current — a high lithium-ion transference number that indicates the framework’s channels and charged surfaces are indeed preferentially shepherding lithium rather than the counterions left behind by the exchange process. artigo.texto: Amazon investirá US$ 1 bilhão em comunidades próximas a data centers nos EUA A Amazon Web Services investirá mais de US$ 1 bilhão nos próximos cinco anos em comunidades americanas que abrigam seus data centers. A Amazon investirá US$ 1 bilhão nos próximos cinco anos em comunidades dos Estados Unidos que possuem data centers da companhia. O anúncio foi feito nesta sexta-feira (2) pela Amazon Web Services (AWS), divisão de computação em nuvem da empresa, que pretende direcionar os recursos para iniciativas como educação, formação profissional, conservação de água e energia e ampliação do acesso à eletricidade. A decisão ocorre em um momento de rápida expansão da infraestrutura necessária para o desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial. Ao mesmo tempo, a instalação de novos data centers tem provocado questionamentos em diferentes comunidades americanas, principalmente em relação ao consumo de eletricidade e água e aos possíveis impactos sobre os custos dos serviços públicos. Amazon investirá US$ 1 bilhão em iniciativas para comunidades De acordo com a AWS, o investimento anunciado será distribuído ao longo dos próximos cinco anos e terá como destino regiões americanas onde a empresa mantém centros de processamento de dados. Os recursos deverão financiar projetos definidos a partir das necessidades locais. Entre as áreas citadas pela companhia estão educação, capacitação profissional, acesso à energia, conservação de água e iniciativas relacionadas à eficiência energética. A estratégia representa uma tentativa de ampliar os benefícios econômicos e sociais associados à presença dos data centers nas comunidades. Essas estruturas são fundamentais para o funcionamento de serviços digitais e, com o crescimento da inteligência artificial, passaram a ter papel ainda mais importante na infraestrutura tecnológica. Consumo de água ganha destaque no plano da AWS Além do aporte financeiro, a AWS apresentou um compromisso relacionado ao uso de recursos hídricos. A empresa pretende fazer com que todos os seus data centers sejam positivos em relação à água até 2030. Na prática, a companhia afirma que pretende devolver às comunidades um volume de água maior do que aquele consumido por suas operações. Segundo a AWS, o avanço em direção à meta já alcançou aproximadamente 75%. A questão é relevante porque o funcionamento de grandes instalações de processamento exige sistemas capazes de controlar a temperatura dos equipamentos. Dependendo da tecnologia utilizada e das condições locais, isso pode aumentar a demanda por água e energia. Com a expansão da inteligência artificial, a necessidade de infraestrutura computacional também cresce. Por isso, o debate sobre como abastecer esses centros sem pressionar excessivamente os recursos disponíveis ganhou espaço nos Estados Unidos. Data centers enfrentam oposição em comunidades americanas O anúncio da Amazon acontece em meio a uma reação contrária à expansão de data centers em diferentes partes dos Estados Unidos. Moradores e autoridades locais têm levantado preocupações sobre o aumento da demanda por eletricidade, o consumo de água e possíveis reflexos nas contas de serviços públicos. A AWS informou que mais de 100 propostas de moratória envolvendo data centers estavam sendo consideradas em diferentes localidades do país. As iniciativas mostram que a expansão da infraestrutura tecnológica não ocorre sem resistência. A Amazon também utilizou seu comunicado para responder às críticas relacionadas aos impactos ambientais, energéticos e econômicos das instalações. A empresa defende que a ampliação dos data centers é necessária para atender ao crescimento da computação em nuvem e, principalmente, da inteligência artificial. O desafio para as companhias do setor é conciliar a necessidade de aumentar a capacidade de processamento com as condições e limitações das regiões escolhidas para receber os empreendimentos. Amazon já destinou US$ 276 bilhões para data centers A dimensão da expansão da infraestrutura da Amazon pode ser observada pelos investimentos realizados anteriormente. Segundo a companhia, foram destinados US$ 276 bilhões a data centers entre 2011 e 2025. A empresa possui grandes projetos ou ampliações em andamento em vários estados americanos. Entre os locais mencionados estão Indiana, Louisiana, Carolina do Norte, Virgínia e Mississippi. Os investimentos estão ligados ao crescimento da AWS e à necessidade de oferecer capacidade computacional para empresas, governos e outros clientes. Com a popularização de ferramentas de inteligência artificial, a demanda por processamento e armazenamento de dados aumentou ainda mais. Além da infraestrutura física, a instalação de data centers movimenta fornecedores, trabalhadores e serviços locais. A Amazon agora pretende ampliar esse impacto por meio dos novos investimentos diretamente direcionados às comunidades. CEO da AWS defende expansão diante da corrida pela IA O presidente-executivo da AWS, Matt Garman, afirmou que existe uma necessidade urgente de ampliar a capacidade dos data centers diante da competição internacional pelo desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial. Segundo o executivo, outros países também reconhecem os possíveis benefícios econômicos e estratégicos da tecnologia. Na avaliação apresentada por Garman, as nações que conseguirem ocupar posições de liderança na inteligência artificial terão influência sobre a evolução desse setor e poderão aproveitar seus resultados. A declaração ajuda a explicar por que a Amazon continua aumentando seus investimentos em infraestrutura mesmo diante da oposição enfrentada em algumas localidades. A expansão da inteligência artificial exige centros capazes de processar grandes volumes de informações e executar modelos cada vez mais complexos. Os data centers, portanto, formam uma das bases físicas dessa transformação tecnológica. artigo.texto: Canada is exploring a new policy framework that could let Canadian companies participate in international carbon markets by trading internationally transferred mitigation outcomes (ITMOs). The federal government announced the initiative on September 24, saying an ITMO framework could attract investment into Canadian climate projects, expand demand for carbon removal and nature-based solutions, and create new export opportunities for Canadian companies. The move comes as international carbon markets develop under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. At the same time, countries and companies are looking for ways to finance emissions reductions and carbon removals as they work toward net-zero targets. For Canada, the opportunity is particularly significant because the country combines large natural resources, geological storage capacity, clean electricity and established expertise in energy and industrial infrastructure. Canada’s Emissions Create a Large Decarbonization Challenge Canada still has a substantial emissions-reduction challenge. The country emitted about 685 million metric tons (Mt) of greenhouse gases in 2024, excluding emissions and removals from the land-use, land-use change and forestry sector. That was down 0.3% from 2023 and 10.3% below 2005 levels. Oil and gas remained Canada’s largest source of emissions. The sector accounted for 208 Mt in 2024, although emissions have declined from their 2014 peak. Electricity emissions have fallen much more sharply, dropping 57% between 2005 and 2024 as Canada reduced coal-fired generation. - Canada’s government projects that emissions could fall to 600 Mt by 2030 under its “With Measures” scenario. Under a more ambitious “With Additional Measures” scenario, emissions could reach 546 Mt by 2030. These figures show why Canada will need a combination of emissions reductions, carbon removal and other climate solutions to reach net zero. An international market could provide another source of capital for some of those activities. What Are ITMOs and Why Do They Matter? ITMOs are internationally transferred mitigation outcomes created under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement. In simple terms, one country can authorize the transfer of an emissions reduction or removal to another country under a cooperative approach. The receiving country can then use the mitigation outcome toward its climate target, subject to the applicable Article 6 accounting rules. The system is designed to prevent the same emissions reduction from being counted toward the climate targets of both countries. This process, known as a corresponding adjustment, is central to maintaining the environmental integrity of international transfers. Canada’s proposed framework would establish how these transfers could operate in the Canadian context. The government said it will work with provinces and territories, Indigenous organizations and other stakeholders while developing the potential framework. It also said any ITMO trading would have to follow Article 6 rules, including requirements related to additionality, verification, permanence and avoiding double counting. International Carbon Markets Are Expanding Canada is considering the framework as carbon pricing and carbon-credit systems expand globally. The World Bank’s 2026 State and Trends of Carbon Pricing report found that 87 carbon-pricing policies were operating worldwide, seven more than the previous year. Direct carbon pricing now covers nearly 30% of global greenhouse gas emissions, while carbon pricing generated more than $107 billion in public revenue in 2025. The broader carbon-credit market is also attracting investment. The World Bank estimates that annual capital committed to future carbon-credit projects ranged from $12 billion to $16 billion in 2025. The estimated annual value of traded carbon credits was about $535 million in 2024, although this figure covers a narrower segment of the overall carbon market than carbon taxes and emissions trading systems. The growth opportunity extends beyond today’s market. The World Bank’s international carbon-market research has highlighted the potential for carbon markets to mobilize climate finance, particularly where domestic public funding cannot cover the investment needed for emissions reductions and removals. Other market research has projected that voluntary carbon-credit demand could grow several-fold by 2030, while the World Bank’s Emission Reduction Program has cited estimates of a $10 billion to $40 billion voluntary carbon market by 2030 under one industry scenario. This expanding market could create opportunities for countries that can supply credible emissions reductions and carbon removals. Canada Sees Carbon Removal as an Economic Opportunity Carbon removal is one area where Canada could potentially benefit from international demand. - Carbon Removal Canada has estimated that a large-scale domestic carbon removal industry could generate significant economic activity by 2050. - Its earlier modelling suggested that a Canadian industry capable of removing more than 300 Mt of CO₂ annually could create more than 330,000 jobs and add about $143 billion to GDP. - More recent modelling from the organization estimates that carbon removal could add $78 billion to Canada’s annual GDP by 2050 and create or support about 300,000 jobs. Canada has several resources that could support this expansion. These include geological formations suitable for CO₂ storage, clean electricity, agricultural and forestry resources, industrial infrastructure and a workforce with experience in engineering, energy and large-scale construction. Carbon removal technologies such as direct air capture and bioenergy with carbon capture and storage could therefore become part of Canada’s emerging clean-technology export industry. artigo.texto: A Amazon Web Services (AWS), empresa de computação em nuvem da gigante de tecnologia e comércio eletrônico Amazon, anunciou em 2 de outubro que investirá mais de US$ 1 bilhão nos próximos cinco anos em comunidades locais onde seus data centers estão localizados nos EUA, além de se comprometer a abordar o impacto de seus data centers no fornecimento de eletricidade e água nessas áreas. A Amazon investirá US$ 1 bilhão em locais nos EUA onde construirá centros de dados. A AWS está investindo mais de US$ 1 bilhão nos próximos cinco anos em comunidades próximas aos seus data centers nos EUA, com foco em educação, energia, água e treinamento profissional para mitigar o impacto local de suas operações. A Amazon afirma ter investido US$ 276 bilhões em infraestrutura de data centers entre 2011 e 2025, além de estar realizando uma série de projetos de grande escala e expandindo suas operações em diversos estados, incluindo Indiana, Louisiana, Carolina do Norte, Virgínia e Mississippi. Segundo a AWS, o pacote de investimentos comunitários anunciado recentemente inclui financiamento para educação , formação profissional, garantia de acesso a energia acessível, conservação de água e energia, e outras prioridades específicas das localidades onde os centros de dados da AWS estão situados. Os centros de dados — que fornecem o poder computacional para treinar e operar modelos de inteligência artificial (IA) — estão enfrentando reações negativas de moradores locais nos Estados Unidos devido a preocupações com o aumento do consumo de eletricidade, o aumento dos custos de serviços públicos e outros impactos locais. Em um comunicado, a AWS tentou rebater as críticas dirigidas aos seus centros de dados em relação aos seus impactos ambientais, energéticos e econômicos . O CEO da AWS, Matt Garman, enfatizou a urgência de expandir a infraestrutura de data centers hoje, observando que os EUA não são o único país a perceber os benefícios econômicos e de segurança nacional da IA, e afirmou que as nações líderes em IA serão as que moldarão e colherão o maior valor dessa tecnologia. Além disso, a AWS está comprometida em devolver à comunidade mais água potável do que a consumida por seus data centers até 2030. A AWS afirma já ter atingido 75% dessa meta.
